pois.name: Puerto de la Cruz Botanical Garden
pois.shortDescription: The oldest botanical garden in the Canaries — founded by King Carlos III in 1788 to acclimatise tropical plants, with over 3,000 species from around the world
pois.description:
The **Jardín de Aclimatación de La Orotava**, commonly known as the Puerto de la Cruz Botanical Garden, is one of the most historically significant gardens in Spain. Founded in **1788 on the orders of King Carlos III**, its original purpose was to acclimatise tropical plants brought from the Americas, Asia and Africa before sending them to the Royal Botanical Garden in Madrid — a botanical «waiting room» for species that had never set foot on European soil.

### History and Mission
The garden was created at the height of the Enlightenment, when Spain was travelling the world collecting scientific specimens for its herbaria and royal gardens. The exceptional climate of northern Tenerife — mild, humid and frost-free — made it the ideal place to acclimatise tropical plants that would otherwise perish on the continent. More than two centuries later, the garden remains a botanical research centre under the stewardship of the **Spanish Ministry of Agriculture**.

### The Collection
In just **20,000 m²**, more than **3,000 plant species** from every continent are concentrated:
- 🌴 Palms, tree ferns and cycads from tropical America
- 🌺 Orchids, bromeliads and carnivorous plants
- 🌿 Endemic Canarian and Macaronesian flora
- 🎋 Giant bamboos, baobabs and species from equatorial Africa
- 🌳 Centenary trees over 200 years old

### The Giant Fig Tree
The garden's undisputed emblem is its **century-old Ficus benjamina**: a tree of extraordinary dimensions whose aerial roots have created over time a botanical labyrinth that looks like something from an adventure film. It is impossible not to stop and stare.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Calle Retama 2, Puerto de la Cruz
- 🕙 Daily **9:00–18:00** (until 19:00 in summer)
- 💶 **Entry fee applies** — check current prices on the official website · Free under 12
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1–1.5 hours**
- 🚌 Bus from Puerto de la Cruz centre: **Line 101**

### Recommendation
Visit in the morning for the best light through the vegetation. The temperature inside the garden is always cool — perfect even on the hottest days in the north. Ideal combined with the **Puerto de la Cruz** town centre and the Martiánez Lake promenade. With children, the garden is an unbeatable natural exploration experience.

pois.name: Palmetum of Santa Cruz
pois.shortDescription: Europe's most important palm collection — 12 hectares built on a former landfill site with over 800 palm species from around the world
pois.description:
The **Palmetum of Santa Cruz de Tenerife** is one of the most extraordinary botanical gardens in Europe and the **continent's most complete palm collection**. Inaugurated in **2014** after more than 20 years of work, its story is as remarkable as its contents: it was built on Santa Cruz's former **municipal landfill**, transforming 12 hectares of waste into one of the world's most valuable gardens.

### A Miracle of Regeneration
Over two decades, the Palmetum team deposited layer upon layer of soil, compost and substrate over the old landfill waste, creating the growing medium needed to host palms from every corner of the planet. The result is an unprecedented story of ecological regeneration in Spain and a world-leading example of converting degraded land into natural heritage.

### The Collection
With over **2,500 specimens** of more than **800 palm species** from five continents, the Palmetum organises its collection by geographic area:
- 🌴 **Americas area**: palms from tropical and subtropical America
- 🌴 **Africa and Madagascar area**: the most singular palms from the African continent, including the legendary **Madagascar palm** (*Ravenea rivularis*)
- 🌴 **Asia and Pacific area**: from the palms of Borneo to those of the Pacific islands
- 🌴 **Canaries and Macaronesia area**: the Canarian palm (*Phoenix canariensis*) in its natural habitat
- 🏞️ **Central lake**: with flamingos and ducks in a setting of great scenic beauty

### The Viewpoints
The garden has several viewpoints with panoramic views over the **Tenerife Auditorium**, the Atlantic and Teide. The combination of palms in the foreground with the Auditorium behind is one of the most singular photographs you can take in Santa Cruz.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Avenida de la Constitución, Santa Cruz (next to the Auditorium)
- 🕙 Daily **10:00–18:00**
- 💶 **Entry fee applies** — check current prices on the official website · Free under 12
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1.5–2 hours**
- 🚋 Tram L1 (stop **Intercambiador** or **Auditorio**) + 5-min walk

### Recommendation
Ideal combined with the **Tenerife Auditorium** and the seafront promenade. The best light for photographing the palms is in the afternoon, when the sun illuminates them from the west. With children, the flamingo lake and the paths between giant palms create a memorable experience.

pois.name: Mariposario del Drago — Butterfly House
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's tropical butterfly garden — hundreds of exotic species fly free among tropical plants next to the Millenary Dragon Tree in Icod
pois.description:
The **Mariposario del Drago** is one of the most enchanting natural spaces in Tenerife: a closed tropical garden where hundreds of **exotic butterflies from around the world** fly freely among orchids, heliconias and tropical plants. Located in **Icod de los Vinos**, just metres from the famous Millenary Dragon Tree, it is an essential visit for families and for anyone seeking a different natural experience.

### The Experience
As you step through the butterfly house door you enter a tropical microclimate: warm temperature, high humidity and a lush garden where butterflies flutter around you, land on flowers and — frequently — on your arms, hands or shoulders. The experience of having a tropical butterfly settle on your skin is something not easily forgotten — especially for young children.

### The Butterflies
- 🦋 **Tropical species** from Asia, Central America and Africa
- 🦋 Large diurnal butterflies with spectacular colours
- 🦋 The full life cycle on display: eggs, caterpillars, chrysalises and adults
- 🦋 New hatchings virtually every day

Among the most striking species are the **Blue Morpho** from tropical America, **Owl butterflies** (*Caligo*) with 15 cm wingspans, and several species of **Asian Papilio** with tailed hindwings.

### The Tropical Garden
The butterflies live surrounded by a **selection of host and nectar plants** recreating their natural habitat: heliconias, anthuriums, passionflowers, tropical orchids and a collection of tropical plants that is worth visiting in its own right.

### Perfect Combination
The butterfly house is located **just metres from the Millenary Dragon Tree** — visiting both together forms one of the most complete excursions in northern Tenerife. The historic old town of Icod de los Vinos, with its wine cellars and the Church of San Marcos, rounds off the day.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Calle San Sebastián, Icod de los Vinos (next to the Dragon Tree)
- 🕙 Daily **9:30–18:00**
- 💶 **Entry fee applies** — check current prices on the official website · Free under 4
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **45 min – 1 hour**
- 📸 Mid-morning light is best for photographing butterflies

### Recommendation
Wear brightly coloured clothing — butterflies are attracted to vivid colours and you'll have a much better chance of them landing on you. Perfect for families with young children: the experience of interacting with free-flying tropical butterflies is magical at any age. Combine with the Dragon Tree (entrance right next door) and Icod's old town for a complete morning out.

pois.name: Parque García Sanabria
pois.shortDescription: The largest urban garden in the Canary Islands — 7 hectares in the heart of Santa Cruz with an exceptional open-air international sculpture collection
pois.description:
**Parque García Sanabria** is the largest urban park in the Canary Islands and one of the most cherished corners of Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Inaugurated in **1926** and named after the mayor who championed its creation, Emilio García Sanabria, this green lung of **73,000 m²** in the heart of the capital is the quintessential meeting place for locals — and a welcome surprise for any visitor who stumbles upon it.

### An Open-Air Sculpture Museum
What makes Parque García Sanabria truly singular is not just its tropical plants or fountains, but its **permanent international sculpture collection**: since 1973, the city has hosted the biennial **International Open-Air Sculpture Competition of Santa Cruz de Tenerife**, and the winning works remain in the park permanently. Today, walking its paths is like browsing decades of international contemporary art amid the greenery: works by artists from across the world stand alongside palms, century-old trees and tropical flowers in a unique combination.

### The Vegetation
The park houses an extraordinary collection of tropical and subtropical plants from every continent:
- 🌴 Palms from the Americas, Africa and Asia
- 🌺 Bougainvilleas, hibiscus and flame trees in permanent bloom
- 🌳 Century-old shade trees of enormous size
- 🌿 Themed gardens with aromatic and medicinal plants
- 🏞️ Ornamental fountains and ponds

### The Luminous Fountain
The large **central fountain**, with its water and light displays, is the park's most iconic feature and the favourite meeting point for families and visitors. At night, when the park is lit up and the fountain springs to life, the atmosphere is especially magical.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Rambla del General Franco, Santa Cruz de Tenerife (city centre)
- 🕙 Open **24 hours** — free access all year round
- 💶 **Free entry**
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1 hour**
- 🚋 Tram L1, stop **García Sanabria** (direct access)
- 🧒 Children's playground inside

### Recommendation
Ideal for a leisurely stroll before or after lunch — the park is surrounded by restaurants and terraces. In spring and summer the vegetation is at its most vibrant. Perfect combined with the **Mercado de Nuestra Señora de África** (5 minutes' walk) and a stroll along the Rambla de Santa Cruz.

pois.name: Anaga Rural Park
pois.shortDescription: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve at the northern tip of Tenerife — the world's most extensive laurel forest, dramatic ravines and timeless rural villages dating back 20 million years
pois.description:
**Anaga Rural Park** is one of the most extraordinary natural spaces not just in the Canaries, but on the entire planet. Declared a **UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2015**, this mountain massif occupying the northeastern tip of Tenerife is home to the **most extensive and best-preserved laurel forest in the world** — a relict ecosystem from the Tertiary era that existed across Europe and North Africa **20 million years ago**, before the ice ages wiped it from the continental map. In Anaga it survived thanks to the special microclimate of northern Tenerife.

### The Laurel Forest: A Prehistoric Wood
Walking through Anaga's forest is, quite literally, travelling back in time. The trees — laurels, tiles, viñátigos, hollies and fayas — are draped in moss and lichen, and their branches intertwine above the paths to create tunnels of vegetation of hypnotic beauty. The permanent humidity and mist that envelops the massif give the landscape an almost magical quality, especially at sunrise.

Key species of the laurisilva:
- 🌿 **Canarian laurel** (*Laurus novocanariensis*) — the emblematic tree
- 🌿 **Til** (*Ocotea foetens*) — prized for its beautifully grained timber
- 🌿 **Viñátigo** (*Persea indica*) — a relative of the avocado
- 🌿 **Faya** (*Myrica faya*) — a shrub that colonises the ravines

### The Ravines and Landscape
Anaga is a land of **rugged and dramatic relief**: sharp ridges plunging steeply to the sea, deep ravines separating isolated villages, and cliffs dropping into the Atlantic. The views from the ridgelines are absolutely spectacular — you can see simultaneously the north and south coasts of Tenerife, Teide in the background, and on clear days even Gran Canaria and La Gomera.

### The Rural Villages
Tucked between the forest are small rural settlements of exceptional authenticity — **Taganana, Las Carboneras, El Bailadero, Chamorga** — where time seems to have stood still. Difficult to reach, with narrow winding roads, they are home to families who have lived for generations from farming and fishing.

### Must-Do Trails
- 🥾 **Cruz del Carmen → Las Carboneras** (9 km, through the heart of the laurel forest)
- 🥾 **Roque de Taborno** (viewpoint with 360° views over the ravines)
- 🥾 **Bosque de los Catalanes** (short route through century-old trees)
- 🥾 **Chinamada** (cave-house village accessible only on foot)
- 🥾 **Playa de Benijo** (descent through a ravine to a wild black-sand beach)

### Wildlife
- 🦜 **Bolle's pigeon** and **white-tailed laurel pigeon** — endemic pigeons of the laurel forest, endangered
- 🦎 Canarian lizard, gecko and several endemic lizard species
- 🦋 Canarian endemic butterflies

### Practical Information
- 📍 Visitor Centre: **Cruz del Carmen** (TF-12, Las Mercedes)
- 🕙 Visitor centre: **9:00–17:00** (closed Mondays)
- 💶 **Free entry** · Parking at Cruz del Carmen
- 🚌 Bus from Santa Cruz: **Line 75** (to Las Mercedes / Cruz del Carmen)
- ⏱️ Variable: from 1 hour (viewpoint) to a full day (long trails)

### Recommendation
Avoid the middle of the day in summer — Anaga's trails have little shade outside the forest and the heat can be intense. Bring a light layer even in sunshine: mist can roll in within minutes and drop the temperature significantly. Sunrise at Cruz del Carmen, with a sea of clouds rolling over the forest, is one of the most breathtaking visual experiences in Tenerife.

pois.name: Teide National Park
pois.shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage Site and Spain's most visited national park — the Teide volcano at 3,718 m, the Las Cañadas caldera and one of the world's finest stargazing skies
pois.description:
**Teide National Park** is, quite simply, one of the most extraordinary places in Spain and the world. A **UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007**, this park of nearly 19,000 hectares in the heart of Tenerife is dominated by **Teide**, whose **3,718 metres** above sea level make it the highest volcano in Spain, the tallest peak in the entire Atlantic and the third largest volcano on Earth measured from its oceanic base.

It is also **Spain's most visited national park** and one of the most visited in Europe — and for good reason: the landscape it offers is unlike anything else on the continent.

### The Volcano and Caldera
Teide is not simply a volcano: it is the result of millions of years of eruptions that have shaped a landscape of extraordinary variety and beauty. The **Las Cañadas caldera** — a circular depression 16 km in diameter formed by the collapse of the ancient volcanic structure — is the setting in which the park sits. Within it, fields of solidified lava, secondary volcanic cones, and bizarrely shaped rocks and spires create a landscape that looks like another planet.

**Essential geological landmarks:**
- 🌋 **Roques de García** — 8-million-year-old volcanic formations, the park's most photographed
- 🌋 **Pico Viejo** — the park's second volcano, with an 800 m wide caldera
- 🌋 **Minas de San José** — fields of lapilli and pumice in extraordinary colours
- 🌋 **El Portillo** — northern gateway to the park, with visitor centre
- 🌋 **La Fortaleza** — impressive 2,159 m rock with views over the caldera

### The Cable Car
The **Teide Cable Car** ascends from 2,356 m to 3,555 m in just 8 minutes, offering one of the most breathtaking perspectives in the Canaries: a sea of clouds beneath your feet, the Atlantic islands on the horizon and the Teide summit above your head. To reach the exact summit (3,718 m), a **free permit** is required, which must be booked in advance on the national parks website.

### Unique Flora
The park is home to plant species found nowhere else on Earth:
- 🌺 **Red tajinaste** (*Echium wildpretii*) — Tenerife's emblematic flower, up to 3 m tall, blooms May–June
- 🌼 **Teide violet** (*Viola cheiranthifolia*) — the highest-growing plant in all of Spain
- 🌿 **Teide broom** (*Spartocytisus supranubius*) — white-pink shrub that perfumes the park in spring
- 🌱 More than 60 species endemic to the National Park

### The Finest Stargazing Sky
Before dawn or after dusk, Teide National Park reveals its best-kept secret: one of the **purest skies in the northern hemisphere** for astronomical observation. The altitude, absence of light pollution and atmospheric stability of the Canaries have placed Teide among the world's finest natural observatories — the **Teide Observatory** of the IAC (Canary Islands Astrophysics Institute) has been measuring the stars here for decades.

### Highlighted Trails
- 🥾 **Roques de García** (circular, 3.5 km, easy, spectacular)
- 🥾 **Telesforo Bravo** (on-foot ascent to the summit, advance booking required)
- 🥾 **Pico Viejo** (permit required, unique views over the volcano's caldera)
- 🥾 **Montana Blanca → Teide** (ascent route on the south face, 7.3 km, +900 m elevation)

### Practical Information
- 📍 Park centre accessible via **TF-21** from La Orotava / Vilaflor
- 🕙 Park: **open 24 hours** · Cable car: **9:00–16:00** (subject to weather conditions)
- 💶 Park: **free** · Cable car: **entry fee applies** — check current price at telefericoteide.com
- 🔒 Summit permit (3,718 m): **free**, advance booking at reservasparquesnacionales.es
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **half day – full day**
- 🚌 Bus from Puerto de la Cruz or Los Cristianos (seasonal service)

### Recommendation
Take the cable car before 10am to avoid queues and ensure clear visibility before clouds rise from the coast. To see the **sea of clouds** at its most spectacular, arrive at sunrise — it is one of the most hypnotic natural spectacles in the Canaries. In spring (April–June), the flowering tajinaste turns the slopes into a sea of red — a sight of extraordinary beauty.

pois.name: Roques de García
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's most iconic volcanic formations — 8-million-year-old rock spires in the heart of Teide National Park with direct views of the volcano
pois.description:
The **Roques de García** are the most recognisable image of Teide National Park and one of the most photographed volcanic landscapes in all of Spain. These **8-million-year-old** basaltic rock formations — older than Teide itself — rise from the centre of the Las Cañadas caldera like silent witnesses to millions of years of volcanic activity, creating a landscape of such spectacularity it feels like it belongs on another planet.

### Geology: A Story Written in Stone
The Roques de García are not the result of a recent eruption but of **differential erosion** on ancient lava flows: harder material has resisted erosion while the surrounding rock has worn away, leaving exposed these pillars and spires that now tower above the caldera. Their distinctive shapes have their own names:

- 🪨 **La Catedral** — the tallest, most vertical roque, rising like a stone bell tower
- 🪨 **Cinchado** — the balancing rock, the most photographed feature: a multi-metre boulder seemingly suspended impossibly above another
- 🪨 **El Sombrero** — an unmistakable hat-shaped profile visible from the road
- 🪨 **La Ruleta** — an almost artificially circular column

The colour contrasts are extraordinary: the black and ochre of the volcanic rock against the white of the pumice and the red of the lapilli, with the snow-capped Teide behind and the Canarian blue sky above.

### The Circular Trail
The circular footpath around the Roques de García is one of the **easiest and most spectacular walks** in the entire national park:
- 🥾 **Distance**: 3.5 km (circular)
- ⏱️ **Duration**: 1–1.5 hours
- 📈 **Elevation gain**: virtually flat (~50 m)
- ⭐ **Difficulty**: very easy — suitable for all

From the trail the views are breathtaking in every direction: Teide and Pico Viejo to the north, the south wall of the caldera in the distance, and the roques themselves changing shape and perspective with every step.

### The Parador Nacional
Just a few metres from the Roques stands the iconic **Parador Nacional de las Cañadas del Teide** — staying here and waking early to watch the sunrise over the rocks, as Teide turns the sky orange and pink, is an experience few people ever forget.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-21, km 41 — Las Cañadas del Teide
- 🅿️ Free parking next to the roques (limited capacity — arrive early)
- 💶 **Free entry**
- 🕙 Accessible **24 hours** (recommended at sunrise or sunset)
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1–1.5 hours**
- 🧥 Average temperature: **10–15 °C** (bring warm clothing all year round)

### Recommendation
Arrive before 9am or after 5pm to avoid tourist coaches and enjoy the site in peace. The dawn and dusk light turns the roques warm golden colours and creates photographs of exceptional quality. In winter, if Teide has snow, the contrast of white snow against black rock is breathtakingly beautiful.

pois.name: Montaña Amarilla Natural Monument
pois.shortDescription: The yellow volcanic cone of the south coast — a unique ochre-coloured tuff formation unlike anything else in Tenerife, right on the sea at San Miguel de Abona
pois.description:
**Montaña Amarilla** is one of the most striking and least-known natural monuments in southern Tenerife. This cone of **volcanic tuff** in an intense yellow-ochre colour — which gives it its name — is the result of a submarine volcanic eruption that consolidated ash on contact with sea water, creating the distinctive material known as **palagonite** that gives it that unique golden hue.

### A Unique Geology
What sets Montaña Amarilla apart from most Canarian volcanoes is its origin: it is a **hydrovolcanic tuff cone**, formed when hot lava came into contact with sea water during the eruption. This explosive reaction fragmented the volcanic material into fine particles that consolidated in layers, creating the characteristic yellowish tuff. The colour, far from uniform, ranges from pale yellow to deep ochre and reddish brown depending on mineral composition and degree of alteration.

It is designated a **Natural Monument** for its geological and landscape value and is one of the finest examples of hydromagmatic volcanism in the Canary Islands.

### The Coastal Setting
The mountain faces directly onto the sea, next to the **Golf del Sur** development in San Miguel de Abona, creating an extraordinary visual contrast: the yellow of the volcanic rock against the deep blue of the Atlantic. The waters surrounding it are particularly calm and clear, sheltered by the cone's own shape, making them a popular spot for **snorkelling and swimming**.

In the surroundings you can observe:
- 🌊 Coastal volcanic rock formations shaped by marine erosion
- 🐟 Seabeds with colourful fish among the volcanic rocks
- 🦎 Canarian lizard (*Gallotia galloti*) sunbathing on the rocks
- 🌵 Xerophilous vegetation adapted to the dry southern coastline

### The Ascent
You can climb to the summit of Montaña Amarilla via a short, easy path from the base. From the top the views are spectacular:
- The southern coastline of Tenerife with its resorts and the port of Los Abrigos
- The island of Gran Canaria on clear days
- The turquoise waters of the surrounding coast
- The black lava fields that contrast with the yellow of the tuff

### Practical Information
- 📍 Golf del Sur, San Miguel de Abona (TF-655)
- 🅿️ Parking at Golf del Sur beach
- 💶 **Free entry**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day**
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1–1.5 hours**
- 🏖️ Can be combined with swimming at nearby natural pools and beaches

### Recommendation
Ideal combined with a visit to the village of **Los Abrigos** (famous for its fresh fish restaurants) and a swim in the local natural pools. The best light for photographing the mountain is in the morning, when the sun shines directly on the yellow face of the cone. Wear comfortable shoes for the climb and use sun protection — southern Tenerife has very little shade.

pois.name: Montaña Roja Special Nature Reserve
pois.shortDescription: The red volcano above El Médano — a protected 171 m cone beside Tenerife's finest natural beach, nesting ground for the critically endangered Houbara bustard
pois.description:
The **Montaña Roja Special Nature Reserve** is one of the most singular natural spaces in southern Tenerife. This **171-metre** volcanic cone — named after the intense red colour of its rock, the result of iron oxidation in the lava — rises directly from the coastline in the municipality of Granadilla de Abona, next to El Médano, creating one of the island's most spectacular coastal landscapes.

### A Sanctuary for Endangered Wildlife
What elevates Montaña Roja beyond its scenic value is its ecological importance: it is one of the few places in Europe where the **Canarian Houbara bustard** (*Chlamydotis undulata fuerteventurae*) nests — a critically endangered steppe bird that has found in the sandy and rocky terrain around the mountain one of its last refuges in the archipelago. The reserve also protects one of the finest examples of **coastal halophilous vegetation** (salt-tolerant) in Tenerife: tabaibas, coastal cardón cacti, balancones and other plants perfectly adapted to the arid southern coastline.

**Notable wildlife:**
- 🦅 **Canarian Houbara bustard** — critically endangered, nests in the area
- 🦅 **Egyptian vulture** (*Neophron percnopterus*) — endemic Canarian subspecies
- 🐦 Sandpipers, plovers and other wading birds on La Tejita beach
- 🦎 Tenerife lizard (*Gallotia galloti*) on the mountain's rocky walls

### The Mountain
The ascent to the summit of Montaña Roja is a short but rewarding experience:
- 🥾 **Distance**: ~2 km (circular from the base)
- ⏱️ **Duration**: 45 minutes – 1 hour
- 📈 **Elevation gain**: 171 m
- ⭐ **Difficulty**: easy to moderate (steep but safe)

From the summit the views are 360°:
- El Médano and La Tejita beach to the north
- Tenerife South Airport to the west
- The island of Gran Canaria on the horizon
- The black lava fields surrounding the mountain
- The Atlantic in all its splendour at your feet

### La Tejita: Tenerife's Finest Natural Beach
At the foot of Montaña Roja stretches **Playa de La Tejita**, considered by many the best natural sand beach in Tenerife: long, wide, with golden sand and no development whatsoever, protected precisely because it lies within the nature reserve. It is also one of the best **windsurfing and kitesurfing** spots in the entire Atlantic — the southerly wind blows here with the ideal consistency and strength for these sports.

### El Médano
The village of **El Médano** is just a few minutes' walk away: an authentic town without the big hotel chains of southern Tenerife, with tapas bars, beach bars and a relaxed atmosphere that sets it apart from the mass tourism of Los Cristianos or Las Américas.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Playa de La Tejita, El Médano — Granadilla de Abona
- 🅿️ Parking at La Tejita (free, limited in summer)
- 💶 **Free entry**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day**
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **2 hours** (ascent + swim at La Tejita)
- 🌬️ Windy area: not recommended in strong calima conditions

### Recommendation
Sunset from the summit of Montaña Roja, with the sun sinking into the Atlantic and the sky turning red — matching the colour of the very rock beneath your feet — is one of the most beautiful in southern Tenerife. Combine the ascent with a swim at La Tejita and dinner in El Médano for a perfect afternoon. Respect the reserve's signposted paths during the Houbara nesting season (January–July).

pois.name: Barranco del Infierno
pois.shortDescription: The most famous hiking trail in southern Tenerife — a protected ravine with laurel forest, 400 m walls and the only permanent waterfall in the south of the island
pois.description:
The **Barranco del Infierno** (Hell's Ravine) is the most celebrated hiking trail in southern Tenerife and one of the most popular paths in the entire archipelago. This spectacular canyon in the municipality of **Adeje** packs, in just 4.5 km, a biodiversity and scenic beauty that contrasts radically with the sun-and-beach tourism of the nearby coast: at the end of the trail you are rewarded with the **only permanent waterfall in southern Tenerife**, a **nearly 80-metre** drop of water at the bottom of a canyon with vertical walls.

### The Ravine
The Barranco del Infierno is a deep canyon carved over thousands of years by water through the Adeje massif. Its vertical walls reach up to **400 metres** in height at some points, creating a humid and sheltered microclimate where plant species typical of the laurisilva — the prehistoric Tertiary forest — survive in conditions that would be impossible in the arid south of Tenerife. The ravine is declared a **Natural Monument** and access is strictly regulated to preserve the ecosystem.

### Flora
The ravine's microclimate supports an unusual vegetation for the south of the island:
- 🌿 **Laurels, tiles and viñátigos** — trees typical of the humid laurel forest of the north
- 🌵 **Cardón cacti and tabaibas** — on the sunnier, drier walls
- 🌺 **Endemic Lotus and Aeonium** — rock-dwelling species on the cliff faces
- 🌾 **Ferns and mosses** — in the wettest sections near the waterfall
- 🌸 Wild orchids in spring

### Wildlife
- 🦅 **Lesser kestrel** — nests in the vertical walls of the ravine
- 🦎 Tenerife lizard and gecko on the sunny walls
- 🐦 Wild canary, blue tit and Sardinian warbler
- 🦋 Canarian endemic butterflies

### The Waterfall
The goal of the trail is the **Infierno waterfall**: a nearly 80-metre cascade that is at its most spectacular in winter and spring. It is the only permanent water source in arid southern Tenerife, which explains why this ravine has been inhabited since the time of the Guanches — the Canarian aboriginals — who left archaeological evidence of their presence here.

### The Trail
- 🥾 **Distance**: 9 km (4.5 km each way)
- ⏱️ **Duration**: 3–4 hours
- 📈 **Elevation gain**: ~400 m
- ⭐ **Difficulty**: moderate
- 🕙 **Visiting hours**: 8:00–13:00 (last entry 13:00)
- 👥 **Maximum capacity**: 300 people/day (advance booking required)

### Practical Information
- 📍 Calle Barranco del Infierno, 1 — Adeje
- 💶 **Entry fee applies** — check current prices at barrancoDelinfierno.com · Free under 3
- 🔒 **Booking required**: barrancoDelinfierno.com
- 🧥 Wear light clothing but bring a light waterproof — the ravine can be damp inside
- 👟 Hiking footwear essential — the ground can be slippery
- 🚫 Not suitable for pushchairs or people with reduced mobility

### Recommendation
Book at least **1–2 weeks in advance** in high season (November–April) — slots fill up fast. Arrive at the car park 30 minutes before your access time. The light inside the ravine is best at the first morning entry (8am). The final section to the waterfall requires some effort, but the visual reward is entirely worth it.

pois.name: Chinyero Volcano
pois.shortDescription: The last volcano to erupt in Tenerife — the 1909 lava flow remains intact among the pine forest, accessible via a beautiful circular trail in the west of the island
pois.description:
The **Chinyero Volcano** is one of the most singular places in Tenerife: the **last volcano to erupt on the island**, in November **1909**, little more than a century ago. For **10 days** (18–28 November), Chinyero expelled lava, ash and gases that threatened the villages of the northwest — and today, over 100 years on, its black lava flow remains perfectly visible and intact among the Canarian pine forest, as if the eruption had happened yesterday.

### The 1909 Eruption
It was the last historical eruption in Tenerife and one of the most studied in the archipelago. Chinyero opened several emission vents at **1,559 metres** altitude in the Teno massif, in the municipality of Santiago del Teide. The lava advanced northward and northwest, destroying farmland and threatening the villages of El Palmar and Erjos, though causing no fatalities. The Church of Santiago del Teide organised prayers and the lava is said to have stopped miraculously before reaching the village — a story the locals still recount with pride.

### The Volcanic Landscape
The result of that eruption is one of the **youngest and best-preserved lava fields in the Canaries**: tongues of black lava stretching between the pine trees, their original morphology virtually intact. You can make out:
- 🌋 **Pahoehoe lava** — smooth, rope-like solidified flows
- 🌋 **Aa lava** — rough, jagged, scoriaceous flows, harder to walk on
- 🌋 **Hornitos** — small secondary cones formed during the eruption
- 🌋 **Lava tubes** — conduits through which lava flowed beneath an already-solidified crust

Among the cracks and hollows of the lava, pioneer vegetation of great ecological value has been colonising: lichens, mosses and the first vascular plants initiating the ecological succession towards forest.

### The Canarian Pine Forest
The volcano is surrounded by one of the **densest and most beautiful Canarian pine** (*Pinus canariensis*) forests in western Tenerife. The Canarian pine is a species unique in the world, capable of resprouting after a fire thanks to dormant buds beneath the bark — a perfect adaptation to the volcanic activity and fires that characterise the Canaries. Walking among these century-old pines with the scent of resin and pine needle carpet underfoot is an experience of absolute tranquility.

### The Circular Trail
- 🥾 **Distance**: ~8 km (circular)
- ⏱️ **Duration**: 3–4 hours
- 📈 **Elevation gain**: ~300 m
- ⭐ **Difficulty**: moderate
- 🚗 Start: recreational area next to TF-82, between Santiago del Teide and Icod

### Practical Information
- 📍 Área recreativa Chinyero — TF-82, km 31 (Santiago del Teide municipality)
- 💶 **Free entry**
- 🅿️ Free parking at the recreational area
- 🧥 Average temperature: **15–20 °C** — bring a light layer
- 📱 No mobile signal along most of the route

### Recommendation
This is one of the least crowded trails in Tenerife — a gem for those seeking authentic nature well away from tourist circuits. It pairs perfectly with a visit to the **Millenary Dragon Tree in Icod de los Vinos** (20 minutes by car) for a complete day in the north-west of the island. Best visited in spring and autumn.

pois.name: Malpaís de Güímar
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's most extensive lava field — a 10 km² Special Nature Reserve in the southeast with unique endemic flora and views over the Güímar Valley
pois.description:
The **Malpaís de Güímar** is one of the least known and most authentic natural spaces in Tenerife. Declared a **Special Nature Reserve**, this vast lava field of more than **10 km²** in the municipality of Güímar is the result of successive volcanic eruptions that shaped the southeast of the island, leaving a landscape of black rock, volcanic scoria and solidified flows over which exceptional endemic Canarian flora has flourished.

### A Pioneer Ecosystem
The term «malpaís» — literally «badlands» — describes the inhospitable, difficult-to-cross aspect of these lava fields. Yet far from being a dead landscape, the Malpaís de Güímar is a living and dynamic ecosystem where nature has been colonising the rock for hundreds of years:

**Notable endemic flora:**
- 🌵 **Canarian cardón** (*Euphorbia canariensis*) — the most emblematic endemic cactus of the Canaries, reaching 4–5 metres in height
- 🌿 **Sweet tabaiba** (*Euphorbia balsamifera*) — a low shrub covering much of the malpaís
- 🌱 **Wild tabaiba** (*Euphorbia regis-jubae*) — with green stems and yellow flowers
- 🌺 **Verode** (*Kleinia neriifolia*) — endemic succulent with yellow flowers
- 🌿 **Balancón** (*Zygophyllum fontanesii*) — coastal halophilous plant
- 🌸 Numerous species of **Aeonium** and rock lichens

**Wildlife:**
- 🦎 **Tenerife lizard** (*Gallotia galloti*) — abundant throughout the malpaís
- 🐦 **Common kestrel**, **Sardinian warbler** and other rock-dwelling birds
- 🦎 **Tenerife gecko** in the lava cracks
- 🦋 Several Canarian endemic butterfly species

### The Landscape
What makes the Malpaís de Güímar special is the combination of natural elements:
- **Black lava** from historical flows, still recognisable in their different morphologies
- **Cardón cacti** and **tabaibas** rising among the rock like a forest of Canarian succulents
- **Views** over the Güímar Valley — one of the most fertile valleys in eastern Tenerife
- The **coast** bordering the malpaís to the east, with cliffs and volcanic stone beaches
- Proximity to the **Pirámides de Güímar** — the enigmatic stepped structures studied by Thor Heyerdahl

### The Trails
Several waymarked paths allow you to explore different areas of the malpaís:
- 🥾 **Coastal trail** — runs along the sea alongside the malpaís
- 🥾 **Inner malpaís trail** — passes among the cardón cacti and lava flows
- 🥾 **Valley viewpoint** — access to panoramic views over Güímar
- ⏱️ Variable duration: from 1 hour to half a day depending on the route chosen

### Practical Information
- 📍 Güímar, Tenerife — access via TF-28 or TF-612
- 💶 **Free entry**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day**
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1.5–2 hours**
- 👟 Closed, sturdy footwear — lava can be very sharp
- ☀️ Little shade: bring sun protection and water

### Recommendation
Combine the malpaís visit with the **Pirámides de Güímar** (just a few kilometres away) and a trip down to Güímar port for fresh fish. It is one of the most authentic and least touristy corners of southeastern Tenerife — a space where the island's volcanic nature shows itself in its purest state. Best visited in autumn and winter, when the rains bring the vegetation to life.

pois.name: La Ensillada Special Nature Reserve
pois.shortDescription: One of the most spectacular nature reserves in the Teno Massif — a protected space at the northwest tip of Tenerife with unique ecosystems, endemic flora and panoramic views over the Cliffs of Los Gigantes
pois.description:
The **La Ensillada Special Nature Reserve** is one of the most singular protected spaces in the **Teno Massif** and, by extension, in all of Tenerife. Embedded at the northwestern tip of the island, this reserve occupies a collado — a mountain saddle between two volcanic ridges — at great altitude above the sea, where the Atlantic wind, millennial geology and endemic flora create an ecosystem of exceptional rarity and beauty.

### The Teno Massif: the Oldest Land
The Teno Massif is over **7 million years old** — the oldest territory in Tenerife, formed long before Teide and the rest of the island existed. The La Ensillada Special Nature Reserve occupies one of the highest and most exposed points of this massif, preserving a fragment of volcanic and natural landscape that is irreplaceable. The protection of this space responds to the need to conserve rupestral habitats, endemic flora and the geological integrity of one of the Canaries' most genuine corners.

### The Protected Flora
The reserve hosts flora of great ecological value adapted to the extreme conditions of altitude, wind and volcanic substrate:
- 🌿 **Tabaibas and cardones** (*Euphorbia* spp.) — the shrubs and cacti typical of the Canarian thermophilous zone
- 🌱 **Verode** (*Kleinia neriifolia*) — columnar succulents endemic to the Canaries
- 🌸 **Aeonium** spp. — succulent rosettes growing in the most unlikely crevices of volcanic rock
- 🌿 **Canarian broom** and **thyme** in transition zones
- 🌳 Pockets of **laurel forest** in the most wind-sheltered ravines
- 🌵 Communities of **tabaiba amarga** (*Euphorbia regis-jubae*) of special botanical value

### Wildlife
The reserve's surroundings are home to emblematic species:
- 🦅 **Common kestrel** (*Falco tinnunculus*) — hunting over the open slopes
- 🐦 **Canary Islands stonechat** (*Saxicola dacotiae*) — the most characteristic bird of arid landscapes
- 🦎 **Tenerife lizard** (*Gallotia galloti*) — on sunny crags
- 🐦 **Wild canary** in the shrubs at the bottom of the saddle

### The Views
La Ensillada's position — a saddle open 180 degrees between two ridges — offers panoramas of unrivalled spectacle:
- 🌊 To the south: the **Cliffs of Los Gigantes** plunging into the Atlantic, with La Gomera in the background
- 🌊 To the north: the coast of Buenavista del Norte and **Punta de Teno**
- 🏔️ To the east: Teide dominating the inland horizon
- 🌊 The **Atlantic** stretching in all directions on the clearest days

### The Geology
The reserve's ground is an open book of the volcanic history of northwest Tenerife: superimposed basalt flows, volcanic dykes perpendicular to the slope and pyroclastic projections accumulating unique colourings — blacks, reds, ochres — on which flora adapted to the impossible grows.

### How to Get There
- 🚗 From Santiago del Teide via the **TF-436** (winding mountain road — drive with care)
- 🚗 From Buenavista del Norte via the same TF-436 heading south
- 🥾 Accessible on foot from various trails in the Teno Rural Park

### Practical Information
- 📍 TF-436 — Teno Massif, Santiago del Teide
- 🛡️ **Protected Natural Space** — Special Nature Reserve
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — dawn and dusk are the most photogenic moments
- ☁️ Mist is frequent and adds a dramatic atmosphere to the landscape
- 🌬️ Very strong wind zone on stormy days — warm clothing even in summer

### Recommendation
The La Ensillada Nature Reserve pairs perfectly with a boat trip to the **Cliffs of Los Gigantes**: seeing these volcanic walls first from above — in all their 800-metre verticality — and then navigating at their feet completely changes the perception of this landscape's scale. Allow at least 1 hour in the reserve to explore the surrounding trails and not limit yourself to the viewpoint visible from the road.

pois.name: Cliffs of Los Gigantes
pois.shortDescription: Europe's highest coastal cliffs — vertical walls of up to 800 m dropping straight into the Atlantic on Tenerife's northwest coast, with dolphins and whales in the waters below
pois.description:
The **Cliffs of Los Gigantes** (The Giants) are one of the most awe-inspiring natural spectacles in the Canaries and all of Europe. These walls of black volcanic rock that plunge vertically from heights of up to **800 metres** straight into the Atlantic constitute one of the most dramatic coastal landscapes on the planet — and one that leaves the deepest impression on those who see them for the first time, whether from land or, even better, sailing at their feet.

### The Formation
The cliffs are the result of **marine erosion of the western flank of the Teno Massif**, the oldest of Tenerife's three volcanic massifs at over 7 million years old. For millennia, the Atlantic has relentlessly attacked this wall of volcanic rock, creating cliffs of near-perfect verticality. The black basalt, streaked by the successive lava flows laid down over millions of years of volcanic activity, has a texture and colouring that is unique — especially when the evening light turns it to gold.

### The Dimensions
- 📏 **Maximum height**: up to **800 metres** above sea level
- 📏 **Length**: approximately **5 km** of cliff face
- 🌊 **Sea depth**: up to **60 metres** beneath the walls

### The Experience
There are two ways to experience the Cliffs of Los Gigantes:

**From land:**
- The **La Ensillada** viewpoint (in the Teno Massif) gives the view from above — the full height of the walls, the ocean behind and La Gomera on the horizon
- The seafront promenade of **Puerto de Santiago** lets you see them from the shore

**From the sea (the definitive experience):**
- **Boat trips** from Los Gigantes port are the way to truly understand the scale of these cliffs. Sailing at their feet — looking up at an 800-metre wall that seems to fall towards you — is an experience without equal on the European Atlantic
- Trips normally include **whale and dolphin watching**: the waters off Los Gigantes are one of the best places in Europe to see **short-finned pilot whales** (*Globicephala macrorhynchus*) and **common bottlenose dolphins**, which live here year-round

### The Cetaceans
The deep, sheltered waters in the lee of the cliffs create an exceptional marine ecosystem:
- 🐋 **Short-finned pilot whale** (*Globicephala macrorhynchus*) — permanent resident, groups of 20–40 individuals
- 🐬 **Bottlenose dolphin** (*Tursiops truncatus*) — the most common, sociable and curious around boats
- 🐬 **Common dolphin** (*Delphinus delphis*) — in groups of up to hundreds
- 🐋 **Humpback whale** (*Megaptera novaeangliae*) — seasonal passage
- 🐋 **Sperm whale** (*Physeter macrocephalus*) — in deep waters offshore

### Diving
The waters beneath the cliffs are one of the **best diving spots in Tenerife**: excellent visibility, rich marine life and the unique experience of diving beneath a rock wall that rises 800 metres above your head.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Los Gigantes port — Santiago del Teide
- 🚢 Multiple companies offer boat trips from the harbour
- 💶 Boat trips: **fee applies** — check current prices directly at Los Gigantes harbour
- 🕙 Departures: usually **10:00 and 12:00** (check seasonally)
- 🐋 Cetacean sightings guaranteed on most trips

### Recommendation
Don't settle for the view from land — the boat trip is what transforms Los Gigantes from a «nice landscape» into a «perspective-changing experience». Dolphins surfing the bow wave are an almost guaranteed bonus. Book at least 24–48 hours ahead in high season. If possible, choose a small boat (max. 12 people) for a more intimate and responsible cetacean-watching experience.

pois.name: Mirador de Chipeque
pois.shortDescription: The most spectacular balcony over the Orotava Valley — at 1,700 m among the pines and Teide, with bird's-eye views over Tenerife's most fertile valley
pois.description:
The **Mirador de Chipeque** is one of the most beautiful and least crowded viewpoints in Tenerife. Perched at **1,700 metres altitude** on the TF-24 road that climbs from La Orotava towards Teide National Park, this natural balcony above the **Orotava Valley** offers one of the most spectacular views on the island: Tenerife's most fertile and greenest valley unfolds below you from the slopes of Teide all the way to the sea, with Puerto de la Cruz, the Atlantic and the outlying islands on the horizon.

### The Perspective
What makes Mirador de Chipeque unique is its privileged position: you are high enough to see the valley in its entirety, yet surrounded by Canarian pine forest that frames the view and gives it a scale that higher viewpoints — where there is only lava and rock — simply do not have. The combination of:
- 🌲 Century-old Canarian pines in the foreground
- 🟩 The deep green carpet of the Orotava Valley in the centre
- 🏘️ The rooftops of La Orotava, La Victoria and Tacoronte climbing the hillsides
- 🌊 Puerto de la Cruz and the northern coastline in the background
- 🌍 The Atlantic stretching to the horizon
- 🏔️ Teide above your head, closing the landscape from above

...creates one of the most complete and balanced landscape compositions in all the Canaries.

### The Orotava Valley
The **Orotava Valley** is Tenerife's most fertile valley, irrigated by the water that descends from Teide through a network of galleries and irrigation channels that the Canarians built over centuries. Its slopes are covered in banana plantations, vineyards, potatoes and orchards that give the valley that deep green colour contrasting with the aridity of the rest of the north. From Chipeque you can appreciate its perfect natural amphitheatre shape — an ancient caldera that opened to the sea millions of years ago.

### The Surroundings
Chipeque is set within the **Corona Forestal**, the natural park surrounding Teide. The Canarian pine (*Pinus canariensis*) forest around the viewpoint is one of the densest and most beautiful on the island, with tall specimens creating an atmosphere of silence and tranquility that is hard to find elsewhere in Tenerife. In spring, the ground is carpeted with broom flowers and the air smells of resin.

### The Light Effects
The hour of day radically changes the character of the viewpoint:
- 🌅 **Morning**: side light illuminating the valley from the east, maximum clarity
- ☁️ **Mid-morning**: possible **sea of clouds** filling the valley, leaving only the peaks above
- 🌅 **Afternoon**: golden light intensifying the greens of the valley and the tones of Teide
- 🌃 **Night**: the Corona Forestal sky is exceptional for stargazing

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-24, km 22 — between La Orotava and Teide National Park
- 🅿️ Parking next to the viewpoint (free, limited capacity)
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — best early morning or late afternoon
- 🧥 Temperature: **10–18 °C** depending on season — always cooler than the coast
- 🚗 Car recommended (TF-24 is a well-maintained mountain road)

### Recommendation
Arrive early if you want a chance of seeing the **sea of clouds** filling the valley — the spectacle of building tops and treetops poking through a layer of cloud as white as cotton wool is absolutely surreal. Combine the visit with the drive up to **Teide National Park** (30 minutes further on the same TF-24) for a complete mountain day. Always bring a warm layer, even if the coast is hot.

pois.name: Mirador de Jardina
pois.shortDescription: The first balcony over Anaga forest — panoramic views over Tenerife's oldest massif and the laurel forest from the road climbing from La Laguna
pois.description:
The **Mirador de Jardina** is one of the first and most striking stops on the approach to Anaga Rural Park from San Cristóbal de La Laguna. Set on the TF-13 road at around **700 metres altitude**, this viewpoint offers one of the most complete views over the **Anaga Massif** — the oldest of Tenerife's three great volcanic massifs, at over 7 million years old — before you enter the heart of the forest.

### The Perspective
From Jardina the gaze opens over a landscape of green ridges covered in laurel forest, cascading one after another to the northeast down towards the coast:
- 🌿 The **ocean of laurisilva** covering the Anaga hillsides from the summits to the ravines
- 🌊 The **north coast** of Tenerife, with cliffs dropping to the Atlantic
- 🏘️ The rooftops of **La Laguna** and the Valle de Aguere in the background
- ⛅ Frequently, the **thermal inversion layer** separating the blue sky above from the low clouds below, creating a visual effect of a «floating island» above the sea of clouds

### The Forest Awaiting You
Jardina is the antechamber to Anaga: from here you can see the forest from outside before entering it. The green ridges visible from the viewpoint reveal themselves, once you are walking among them, as a labyrinth of century-old moss-covered trees, cobbled paths and ravines where time seems to have stopped. The viewpoint prepares you visually for what is about to be experienced.

### Surrounding Flora
The immediate surroundings already show the first transition species towards the laurel forest:
- 🌿 **Tree heathers** (*Erica arborea*) — the first trees of the humid forest
- 🌳 **Canarian holly** (*Ilex canariensis*) — evergreen endemic holly
- 🌱 **Ferns** and **lichens** indicating permanent moisture
- 🍃 **Fayas** and **laurels** announcing the entry into the full laurisilva

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-13, km 8 — between La Laguna and Las Mercedes
- 🅿️ Parking area next to the viewpoint (free)
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — best early morning before the mist rolls in
- 🚌 Bus from La Laguna: **Line 75** (towards Cruz del Carmen / Las Mercedes)
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **30–45 minutes**

### Recommendation
Jardina is the perfect stop to pause before entering Anaga: it gives you the overall perspective that you will lose once you are inside the forest. Combine it with the **Mirador de Cruz del Carmen** (15 minutes further on the same road) for two complementary viewpoints — one from outside the forest and one from within. On misty days the atmosphere is especially magical.

pois.name: Mirador Cruz del Carmen
pois.shortDescription: The heart of Anaga Rural Park — the most iconic viewpoint over the laurel forest, with a hermitage, visitor centre and the most breathtaking views over Tenerife's prehistoric forest and north coast
pois.description:
The **Mirador de Cruz del Carmen** is, without doubt, the nerve centre of **Anaga Rural Park** and the place where the massif reveals its full character. At **920 metres altitude** on the TF-12 road (Las Mercedes), this viewpoint combines in a single spot the **Ermita de la Cruz del Carmen** — a small 17th-century chapel with a history tied to the prayers of northern farmers —, a traditional Canarian restaurant, the park's Visitor Centre, and a panorama over the laurel forest that is, quite simply, one of the most beautiful in the Canaries.

### The Landscape
The view from Cruz del Carmen is one of those panoramas that stay with you forever:
- 🌿 The **green sea** of the laurisilva spreading in every direction — the world's most extensive Tertiary forest
- 🌊 The **north coast** of Tenerife tumbling in cliffs into the Atlantic
- ⛅ Frequently a **sea of clouds** covering the valley, leaving only the Anaga peaks emerging like islands
- 🏔️ On clear days, **Teide** in the south, rising above everything
- 🌅 **Sunrise** over the massif, with the sun emerging from the Atlantic to the east, is one of the most spectacular in Tenerife

### The Laurel Forest from Cruz del Carmen
Cruz del Carmen is the starting point for the most important trails in Anaga. The forest surrounding the viewpoint is among the densest and best-preserved in the massif:
- 🌳 Century-old laurels reaching 15–20 metres in height
- 🌿 Tiles and viñátigos with trunks cloaked in deep green moss
- 🍂 The floor carpeted with damp leaf litter and interlacing roots
- 🕊️ The song of the **Bolle's pigeon** and the **white-tailed laurel pigeon** — the two endemic pigeons of the laurel forest, both endangered

### Trails from the Viewpoint
- 🥾 **Cruz del Carmen → El Bailadero** (3 km, along the ridge with views of both coasts)
- 🥾 **Cruz del Carmen → Las Carboneras** (9 km, through the heart of the forest)
- 🥾 **Cruz del Carmen → Chinamada** (8 km, to the cave-house village)
- 🥾 **Bosque de los Catalanes** (2 km circular, perfect for families)

### The Hermitage and Restaurant
The **Ermita de la Cruz del Carmen**, dating from the 17th century, is one of the most picturesque elements of the site. The small restaurant next to the viewpoint serves traditional Canarian dishes — papas arrugadas, ropa vieja, bienmesabe — in a rustic and welcoming setting, perfect for refuelling before or after a trail.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-12 (Las Mercedes) — La Laguna municipality
- 🅿️ Free parking next to the viewpoint
- 💶 **Free access** · Restaurant and shop at visitor centre
- 🕙 Visitor centre: **9:00–17:00** (closed Mondays)
- 🚌 Bus from La Laguna: **Line 75**
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1–3 hours** depending on whether you do a trail or just the viewpoint

### Recommendation
Sunrise at Cruz del Carmen — arriving before the sun comes up and watching as the light gradually illuminates the sea of clouds and the forest — is one of the most impressive natural experiences in Tenerife. Bring warm clothing even on a warm coastal day: at 920 metres in mist, the temperature can drop below 10 °C. Mist and drizzle are not obstacles here: they are part of Anaga's character and create an especially magical atmosphere.

pois.name: Mirador de Cherfe
pois.shortDescription: The balcony over Masca ravine — vertiginous views over the deepest canyon in the Teno Massif, Teide on the horizon and Tenerife's west coast
pois.description:
The **Mirador de Cherfe** is one of the most dramatic and thrilling viewpoints in Tenerife. Perched on the TF-82 road between Santiago del Teide and Tamaimo, this natural balcony over the **Barranco de Masca** — the most spectacular canyon in the Teno Massif — offers a view that takes your breath away: vertical walls dropping hundreds of metres to the ravine floor, the village of Masca clinging to the crags below, and Teide closing the horizon.

### The Masca Ravine from Above
From Cherfe you can grasp in a single glance what makes the Barranco de Masca so special: a system of nested canyons where ravines branch and deepen for kilometres down to the sea. The view reveals:
- 🏔️ Canyon walls with **drops of 400–600 metres** of near-vertical cliff
- 🏘️ The **village of Masca** appearing among the crags below — a handful of houses that seem impossible at that height and in that setting
- 🌿 The hillsides covered in **xerophilous vegetation** — cardón cacti, tabaibas, Canarian palms — alternating with bare rock
- 🌋 **Teide** dominating the eastern horizon in all its grandeur
- 🌊 The **west coast** of Tenerife with the ocean beyond and, on clear days, the silhouettes of **La Gomera** and **La Palma**

### The Village of Masca
Masca is the most inaccessible and most photographed village in the Teno Massif — and one of the most singular in Tenerife. Clinging to a ridge between two ravines at over 600 metres altitude, reached by a single road of tight hairpin bends, Masca maintained for centuries an isolation that has preserved both its architecture and its natural surroundings. From the Mirador de Cherfe you can see it from an external perspective that is rarely appreciated from within the village itself.

### The Teno Massif Landscape
The landscape around Cherfe is the **Teno Massif** at its most untamed:
- 🌵 Giant Canarian cardón (*Euphorbia canariensis*) on the sunny slopes
- 🌴 Canarian palms (*Phoenix canariensis*) in the most sheltered ravines
- 🌿 Tabaibas, verodes and bejeques on the rocky walls
- 🦅 Kestrels and Egyptian vultures soaring above the ravine on thermal currents

### The Masca Trail
Cherfe is also the natural starting point for descending to Masca and accessing the **Barranco de Masca** trail — the descent to the sea that is one of the most spectacular hikes in the Canaries:
- 🥾 **Masca → Masca Beach** (3.8 km, descent only, return by boat)
- ⭐ Moderate to high difficulty — requires booking and a return boat from the beach
- ⏱️ 3–4 hours of descent

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-82, between Santiago del Teide and Tamaimo
- 🅿️ Parking area next to the viewpoint (free)
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — sunset is especially spectacular
- 🌬️ Strong wind area — visibility drops in calima conditions
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **30–45 minutes** (viewpoint only)

### Recommendation
**Sunset from Cherfe** is one of the finest in western Tenerife: the sun sinks into the Atlantic directly above the ravine, lighting the canyon walls in orange and gold as Masca gradually falls into shadow. Arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset to pick your spot. Combine with a visit to **Masca village** (10 minutes on the TF-82) and, if you have the energy and have booked ahead, descend the ravine to the beach for a complete and unforgettable day.

pois.name: Mirador La Garañona
pois.shortDescription: A secret balcony among century-old pines of the Corona Forestal — privileged views over the Orotava Valley and the north coast from the heart of Teide's pine forest
pois.description:
The **Mirador La Garañona** is one of those corners that tourists rarely find and that Tinerfeños keep as a treasure. Nestled within the **Corona Forestal**, the great natural park of Canarian pines surrounding Teide National Park, this viewpoint offers an intimate and silent perspective over the Orotava Valley and the north coast of Tenerife — without the crowds of better-known viewpoints, surrounded only by the sound of wind through the pines and the scent of resin.

### The Setting: The Corona Forestal
The **Corona Forestal** is the natural park that acts as a green belt around Teide National Park, at altitudes between **1,000 and 2,000 metres**. The Canarian pine (*Pinus canariensis*) that dominates this space is one of the most singular plant formations in the world: an endemic species that grows only in the Canaries and has developed extraordinary adaptations to survive fires and volcanic activity — its dormant buds beneath the bark allow it to resprout weeks after being completely burned.

### The Views
From La Garañona the view opens between the pines to the north, with a perspective different from the more popular viewpoints:
- 🌲 **Century-old pines** framing the view in the foreground — a naturally beautiful photographic composition
- 🟩 The **Orotava Valley** unfolding from the slopes of Teide all the way to the coastline
- 🌊 **Puerto de la Cruz** and the north coast gleaming in the background
- 🌍 The **Atlantic** closing the horizon
- ⛅ On winter and spring mornings, the spectacular **sea of clouds** filling the valley

### The Silence of the Forest
What sets La Garañona apart from other viewpoints is the atmosphere around it: the **silence of the pine forest** broken only by the wind, the great spotted woodpecker (*Dendrocopos major thanneri*) hammering some distant trunk, or the flight of a sparrowhawk through the canopy. It is a viewpoint for those seeking contemplation rather than a photo stop — though the photographs it offers are of exceptional quality.

### Wildlife of the Pine Forest
- 🐦 **Tenerife blue chaffinch** (*Fringilla teydea*) — one of the rarest birds in Europe, endemic to Teide's pine forests
- 🐦 **Canarian great spotted woodpecker** (*Dendrocopos major thanneri*) — endemic woodpecker subspecies
- 🦅 **Sparrowhawk** and **goshawk** — forest raptors hunting between the pines
- 🦎 **Tenerife lizard** and **gecko** in the sunny edges of the forest

### Practical Information
- 📍 Corona Forestal, La Orotava municipality — access via TF-21 or TF-24
- 🅿️ Parking area next to the viewpoint (free)
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day**
- 🧥 Temperature: **12–18 °C** — the forest is always cooler than the coast
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **30–45 minutes** + optional walk through the pine forest

### Recommendation
La Garañona is the perfect stop on the way between the north coast and Teide National Park. Pause here for 20–30 minutes before continuing the climb — the transition from coastal heat to pine forest coolness, and the perspective over the valley you have just left behind, is part of the experience of ascending to Teide. If you have time, a short walk through the adjacent pine forest paths is well worth it.

pois.name: Mirador de las Narices del Teide
pois.shortDescription: Teide's volcanic wounds exposed — the spectacular viewpoint over the 1798 secondary craters and the black lava flows that descended to the sea on the southwest flank
pois.description:
The **Mirador de las Narices del Teide** (Teide's Nostrils Viewpoint) is one of the most impressive volcanic observation points in Tenerife. Situated on the TF-38 road that descends from Teide National Park towards Chio and Santiago del Teide, this viewpoint offers an exceptional view of the **Narices del Teide** — the secondary craters and eruptive vents on the southwest flank of **Pico Viejo**, which in the **1798** eruption expelled the most recent lava flows of the Teide volcanic structure.

### The Narices: The Last Great Eruption
In **1798**, the southwest flank of Pico Viejo (Teide's twin volcano within the National Park) opened a series of eruptive vents on its slope that the Canarians nicknamed the **Narices del Teide** — the nostrils of the volcano. For months these vents expelled lava that flowed down the Barranco de las Arenas Negras towards the southwest, reaching the sea and creating new kilometres of lava coastline in what is now the Los Guíos area.

The flows from that eruption — nearly **230 years on** — are still perfectly visible from the viewpoint: tongues of black lava descending the flank of Pico Viejo, their original morphology still intact, contrasting with the ochre and white of the Las Cañadas caldera surrounding them.

### The Geological Spectacle
From the viewpoint you can take in:
- 🌋 The **eruptive vents** of 1798 — secondary craters on the flank of Pico Viejo
- 🌋 The **black lava flows** descending to the southwest, still young at geological scale
- 🌋 **Pico Viejo** (3,135 m) — the park's second volcano, with its enormous 800 m wide caldera
- 🌋 **Teide** in the background in all its monumental grandeur
- 🏔️ The **Las Cañadas caldera** revealed from a completely different angle than usual
- 🌊 The **southwest coast** of Tenerife visible in the background on clear days

### The TF-38: The Road Less Travelled
The TF-38 is the least-used access route to Teide National Park — most visitors enter via the TF-21 from the north or south — which is precisely why it offers the most peaceful and authentic experience. It is a high-mountain road climbing from Santiago del Teide and Chio through the pine forest and lava fields into the national park from the southwest. The Narices viewpoint sits at one of the most spectacular points of this approach.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-38, southwest access to Teide National Park
- 🅿️ Parking area next to the viewpoint (free)
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — mornings offer the best visibility
- 🧥 Temperature: **8–15 °C** — high mountain zone, strong winds possible
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **30–45 minutes**

### Recommendation
If you are visiting Teide National Park, the TF-38 approach from the southwest gives you a completely different perspective on Teide from the usual one: you climb through pines and lava and suddenly the volcano appears from the southwest angle, with the Narices in the foreground and Pico Viejo beside it. It is one of the most cinematic entrances to the park. Combine it with the Chio road and the black lava landscape to understand the volcano from its most intimate and untamed side.

pois.name: Mirador Archipenque
pois.shortDescription: The closest land viewpoint to the Cliffs of Los Gigantes — near-frontal views of the black volcanic walls and the Atlantic from the southern end of Los Gigantes
pois.description:
The **Mirador Archipenque** is the closest land point to the **Cliffs of Los Gigantes** and offers the most different and striking perspective of these volcanic walls: rather than seeing them from above (as from La Ensillada) or from the sea (as on the boat trip), here the cliffs are viewed **almost head-on and at a similar height**, revealing a texture and scale of the rock that no other vantage point can show.

### The Unique Perspective
Archipenque is set on a volcanic promontory to the south of Los Gigantes harbour, at a height that allows you to see the cliffs almost face-on. The view is completely different from that obtained from the Puerto de Santiago seafront promenade:
- 🪨 The **volcanic texture** of the black walls — the layers of basalt laid down over millions of years are perfectly visible
- 📏 The **true scale** of the cliffs — here you feel viscerally that these walls are 600–800 metres high
- 🌊 The **deep dark blue** sea at the foot of the cliffs — waters 40–60 metres deep
- 🌅 **Sunset** lighting the black walls from the west — turning them orange, gold and red
- 🌍 The island of **La Gomera** clearly visible on the horizon — on very clear days also **La Palma** and **El Hierro**

### The Cliffs from Archipenque
What makes this viewpoint special is its position at the southern base of the cliffs: while La Ensillada sees them from above and the boat sees them from below, Archipenque sees them **head-on at mid-height**. This allows you to appreciate:
- The **basalt columns** forming the base of the cliffs
- The **nesting kestrels** and other cliff-dwelling birds in the rock crevices
- The **sea caves** at water level, some accessible only by kayak
- The changing colour of the rock throughout the day — from black to gold to red to orange

### The Setting
The Archipenque viewpoint is surrounded by a coastal volcanic landscape of great beauty: the black lava floor, the coastal xerophilous vegetation — tabaibas, cardón cacti, balancones — and the sound of the sea breaking against the rock create an atmosphere that has very little in common with the mass tourism just a few kilometres away in Los Gigantes and Puerto de Santiago.

### Practical Information
- 📍 Access from Los Gigantes / Puerto de Santiago — Santiago del Teide
- 🅿️ Parking in the vicinity
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — sunset is the highlight
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **45 minutes – 1 hour**
- 🌬️ Area exposed to southwest winds

### Recommendation
Sunset at Archipenque, with golden light lighting the black cliffs almost head-on as the sun sinks into the Atlantic, is one of the most photogenic in all of Tenerife. Combine it with a walk along the Los Gigantes seafront and dinner at the harbour to close the day with a complete experience of the Teno Massif from the sea. For kayak enthusiasts, the zone at the foot of the cliffs is absolutely extraordinary — several local companies organise kayak trips to the sea caves.

pois.name: Mirador de La Ruleta
pois.shortDescription: A silent balcony inside Teide National Park — views over the Las Cañadas caldera and the lava fields from one of the park's least-visited viewpoints
pois.description:
The **Mirador de La Ruleta** is one of those viewpoints in Teide National Park that hurrying visitors tend to drive past — and that those who stop discover as one of the most contemplative and peaceful stops along the entire caldera route. Set on the TF-21 road inside the park, this viewpoint takes its name from the **Roque de La Ruleta**, one of the volcanic formations of the Roques de García whose circular, columnar shape resembles, from a distance, a stone wheel or potter's wheel.

### The Caldera from La Ruleta
From this viewpoint the perspective over the interior of the Las Cañadas caldera differs from the more famous vantage points:
- 🌋 The **lava fields** from different volcanic epochs spreading across the caldera floor
- 🪨 The **Roques de García** visible from an unusual angle — their shapes and silhouettes appreciated in lateral perspective
- 🌋 **Teide** in its full height, dominating the northern horizon
- 🌋 **Pico Viejo** with its large lateral caldera
- 🏔️ The **south wall** of Las Cañadas — the ancient volcanic rock rampart delimiting the caldera to the south
- 🌵 The park's singular flora: **Teide broom**, **tajinaste** (in spring) and **Teide violets** in the crevices

### The Tranquillity
What distinguishes La Ruleta from the park's busiest viewpoints is precisely its **lower visitor numbers**. While the cable car and Roques de García car parks fill up from early morning, La Ruleta is a point where the same volcanic landscape can be contemplated in relative solitude. The silence, broken only by the caldera wind, is an essential part of the experience.

### Surrounding Flora
- 🌿 **Teide broom** (*Spartocytisus supranubius*) — the most abundant white-pink shrub in the park, flowering May–June
- 🌺 **Red tajinaste** (*Echium wildpretii*) — Tenerife's emblematic spring flower on the surrounding slopes
- 🌼 **Teide violet** (*Viola cheiranthifolia*) — growing in rock crevices near the viewpoint
- 🌱 **Codeso del Teide** (*Adenocarpus viscosus*) — yellow high-altitude shrub

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-21 — inside Teide National Park
- 🅿️ Parking area next to the viewpoint (free)
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day**
- 🧥 Temperature: **5–15 °C** depending on season — always colder than the coast
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **30–45 minutes**

### Recommendation
A perfect pause on the park itinerary between the Roques de García and the cable car. Combining La Ruleta with the Roques circular trail (3.5 km) makes a complete morning of low-exertion, high-impact volcanic exploration. On snowy winter days, the contrast of black rock with white snow at the viewpoint has an unmistakably austral beauty.

pois.name: Mirador Pico del Inglés
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's most spectacular 360° viewpoint — at nearly 1,000 m in the heart of Anaga, with simultaneous views of Teide, the Atlantic, La Laguna and the laurel forest in every direction
pois.description:
The **Mirador Pico del Inglés** is, for many who know Tenerife well, the most spectacular viewpoint on the entire island. Its location — at one of the highest points of the **Anaga Massif**, at nearly **1,000 metres** altitude — gives it an unobstructed **360-degree** panorama that takes in virtually the entire geography of Tenerife and much of the surrounding Atlantic. It is one of those places where the true scale of the island becomes clear in a single glance.

### The Name
«Pico del Inglés» — Englishman's Peak — owes its name to the historical custom of British travellers and merchants who, from the 19th century onwards, made the trek on foot or horseback to this point to take in the landscape. The British had a particular fondness for Tenerife (La Laguna was for centuries a regular stop on Atlantic trade routes) and this peak was one of their favourite excursions from the city.

### The 360° Panorama
Standing at Pico del Inglés, a single full turn takes in:
- 🌋 **Teide** to the southwest — Spain's highest volcano rising above the horizon of pines and clouds
- 🌊 The **north coast** of Tenerife with its cliffs and the Atlantic
- 🏙️ **San Cristóbal de La Laguna** and the **Valle de Aguere** spreading to the south and west
- 🌿 The **ocean of laurisilva** of the Anaga Massif in every direction — the world's most extensive Tertiary forest seen from within
- 🌊 The **east coast** of Tenerife with Santa Cruz in the background
- 🌍 On very clear days: **Gran Canaria** to the south, **La Gomera** to the west, even **El Hierro** and **La Palma**
- ⛅ Frequently, the spectacle of the **sea of clouds** — the viewpoint sits above the thermal inversion layer and you can watch the cloud blanket stretch over the valley and coast

### The Forest from Above
From Pico del Inglés, the laurel forest is revealed from its aerial perspective: the canopies of laurels, tiles and fayas create a dense, dark green carpet covering the hillsides in every direction. This view from above — achievable only at the handful of points that rise above the forest — is qualitatively different from walking within it: here you see the true extent of the laurisilva.

### Sunrise and Sunset
Pico del Inglés has a reputation among Tenerife's nature photographers for the quality of its light at the key moments of the day:
- 🌅 **Sunrise**: the sun emerges from the Atlantic to the east directly in front of the viewpoint, illuminating the forest in golden tones and the fog-filled Valle de Aguere
- 🌅 **Sunset**: the sun sets above Teide to the west, with the volcano silhouetted against a red and orange sky

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-12 (Las Mercedes), Anaga — La Laguna municipality
- 🅿️ Free parking next to the viewpoint
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — best at sunrise or sunset
- 🧥 Temperature: **10–18 °C** — the massif is always cooler than the coast
- 🚌 Bus from La Laguna: **Line 75**
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **45 minutes – 1 hour**

### Recommendation
If you had to choose just one viewpoint in Tenerife, this would be one of the strongest candidates. The breadth and variety of the panorama — Teide, Atlantic, forest, city, island, clouds — from a single point is unmatched on the island. Combine it with the **Mirador Cruz del Carmen** (10 minutes on the TF-12) to complete the two finest viewpoints in Anaga. Arrive at sunrise if possible — the spectacle of light breaking over the forest and the valley of clouds is truly extraordinary.
