pois.name: Corona Forestal Natural Park
pois.shortDescription: The largest natural park in the Canaries — 46,000 hectares of Canarian pine forest around Teide, home of the blue chaffinch and a paradise for hikers at 1,000 to 2,000 m altitude
pois.description:
The **Corona Forestal Natural Park** is the largest natural park in the Canary Islands at **46,000 hectares** and the green belt that surrounds Teide National Park, protecting it and creating a transition zone between the coastal world and the volcanic high-mountain world. At altitudes between **1,000 and 2,200 metres**, the Corona Forestal is primarily the domain of the **Canarian pine** (*Pinus canariensis*) — the only pine endemic to the Canaries and one of the most extraordinary trees on the planet.

### The Canarian Pine: A Unique Species
The Canarian pine is, quite simply, one of the most singular trees in the world. Unlike most conifers, it possesses a near-miraculous ability: it can **resprout after a forest fire** thanks to the dormant buds it stores beneath its bark. Weeks after fire has swept through the forest, the charred trunks begin producing new green shoots from the base, trunk and branches — a perfect adaptation to the recurring fires and volcanic activity that characterise the Canarian archipelago.

The Canarian pine also has the longest needles of any European pine — up to 30 cm — and can survive temperatures as low as -15 °C and heavy snowfall, making it the dominant tree at medium-high altitudes in the western Canaries.

### Biodiversity
**Flora:**
- 🌲 **Canarian pine** (*Pinus canariensis*) — dominant between 1,000 and 2,000 m
- 🌿 **Tree heather** (*Erica arborea*) and **faya** (*Myrica faya*) — in transition zones with the laurel forest
- 🌱 **Teide broom** (*Spartocytisus supranubius*) — at higher zones bordering the national park
- 🍄 A great diversity of **fungi and lichens** growing on the pine needle carpet and trunks

**Wildlife:**
- 🐦 **Tenerife blue chaffinch** (*Fringilla teydea*) — one of the rarest birds in Europe, endemic exclusively to the pine forests of Teide and the Corona Forestal. The male has spectacular cobalt-blue plumage; the female is more subdued but equally elusive
- 🐦 **Canarian great spotted woodpecker** (*Dendrocopos major thanneri*) — more often heard than seen
- 🦅 **Sparrowhawk** and **goshawk** — forest raptors
- 🦎 **Tenerife lizard** in sunny clearings between the pines

### The Recreational Areas
The Corona Forestal has numerous **recreational areas** distributed throughout the park, equipped with picnic tables, barbecues, water sources and trail access. Some of the most popular:
- 🌲 **Aguamansa recreational area** — on the north slope, access from La Orotava
- 🌲 **La Caldera recreational area** — near Vilaflor, in the south
- 🌲 **Chinyero recreational area** — next to Chinyero Volcano, in the west
- 🌲 **El Portillo recreational area** — at the border with the National Park

### The Trails
The Corona Forestal is crossed by an extensive network of waymarked paths that allow exploration of the pine forest in all its dimensions:
- 🥾 **Orilla del Bosque trail** — runs along the forest edge with valley views
- 🥾 **Teide trail** — connects park zones with views of the volcano
- 🥾 **GR-131 (Teide Route)** — the inter-island long-distance trail passes through the Corona Forestal

### Practical Information
- 📍 Surrounds Teide National Park — accessible via TF-21, TF-24, TF-38 and TF-28
- 💶 **Free access** on foot and by car
- 🕙 Accessible **all day** — recreational areas open from dawn to dusk
- 🧥 Temperature: **12–22 °C** depending on altitude and season
- ⏱️ Variable: from a 1-hour walk to multi-day routes

### Recommendation
The Corona Forestal is the perfect natural space for those who want authentic, peaceful nature without the mass tourism of Teide National Park. The recreational areas are ideal for families with children. If you are searching for the **blue chaffinch**, your best option is the Aguamansa pine forest in early morning during spring — that is when the male is most active, singing from the tops of the tallest pines.

---

pois.name: Llano de Ucanca
pois.shortDescription: The great interior plain of Las Cañadas del Teide — a volcanic plateau at 2,100 m altitude that feels like another planet, with Teide behind and the Roques de García alongside
pois.description:
The **Llano de Ucanca** is the most extensive and spectacular plain within the **Las Cañadas del Teide caldera** and one of the most awe-inspiring and otherworldly landscapes in all of Spain. At **2,100 metres altitude**, this vast flat space in the heart of Teide National Park is formed by deposits of pumice, lapilli and solidified lava from different eruptive epochs that create a soil of incredible colours: whites, ochres, greys, blacks and reds blending in a unique mineral tapestry.

### The Landscape
The Llano de Ucanca has something of an alien world about it: it is too vast, too silent and too strange to feel like somewhere on Earth. The plain stretches for kilometres with near-perfect horizontality, bordered by the caldera walls to the south and with **Teide** dominating the northern horizon in all its monumentality. At its sides stand the **Roques de García** and the **Parador Nacional de Las Cañadas** — the two most iconic man-made elements in this landscape.

### The Colours of the Ground
What makes the Llano de Ucanca visually unique are its colours:
- ⬜ **White pumice** from Teide's explosive eruptions — areas of an almost blinding white
- 🟤 **Ochre lapilli** — the spongy porous volcanic stone soil typical of Las Cañadas
- ⬛ **Black basaltic lava** from the most recent flows
- 🔴 **Red scoria** oxidised by volcanic iron
- 🟡 **Yellow pumice** from eruptions of differing composition

This colour palette, which changes with the light of the day, is the most characteristic visual hallmark of the Llano de Ucanca and the reason it is one of the most photographed landscapes in Tenerife.

### The Light
The quality of light on the Llano de Ucanca varies extraordinarily by hour:
- 🌅 **Sunrise**: raking pink and orange light sweeping the plain and illuminating the caldera walls from the east
- ☀️ **Midday**: overhead light flattening the landscape and making the pumice shine
- 🌅 **Sunset**: the best light — the sun illuminates Teide from the west, casting long shadows across the plain as the sky blazes orange and red
- 🌃 **Night**: the Llano de Ucanca is one of the park's finest stargazing spots — the sky at 2,100 m, free of light pollution, is exceptional

### The Parador Nacional
Beside the Llano de Ucanca stands the **Parador Nacional de Las Cañadas del Teide**, the only accommodation within the National Park. Staying here and going out before dawn to walk the Llano de Ucanca in absolute silence, with Teide dark against a sky full of stars, is one of the most memorable experiences Tenerife can offer.

### Singular Flora
Despite the extreme conditions — cold, wind, poor soil and drought — the Llano de Ucanca is not devoid of plant life:
- 🌿 **Teide broom** (*Spartocytisus supranubius*) — scattered shrubs that fill with white and pink flowers in May–June
- 🌺 **Red tajinaste** (*Echium wildpretii*) — appears at the edges of the plain, spectacular in spring
- 🌼 **Teide violet** (*Viola cheiranthifolia*) — grows even in the cracks of the most exposed lava

### Practical Information
- 📍 Road TF-21 — inside Teide National Park, next to the Parador
- 🅿️ Parking at the Parador and Roques de García (free)
- 💶 **Free access**
- 🕙 Accessible **24 hours** — especially recommended at sunrise, sunset and night
- 🧥 Average temperature: **5–12 °C** — warm clothing essential at all times of year
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **1–2 hours** (walk across the plain)

### Recommendation
Sunrise on the Llano de Ucanca — arriving before the sun comes up and watching as pink light gradually illuminates Teide and the caldera while the plain remains in shadow — is one of the most powerful visual experiences Tenerife offers. Always combine it with the Roques de García (a few minutes by car) for a complete morning at the heart of the national park. In spring, when the tajinastes and broom are in flower, the landscape takes on an additional dimension of beauty that is almost impossible to describe.

---

🌿 **Responsible tourism in the Canary Islands**
Canarian ecosystems are unique in the world. Small gestures make a big difference:

- 🚶 Stick to marked trails and don't access restricted areas
- 🗑️ Leave no trace — take back what you bring
- 🐋 Keep your distance from wildlife and don't feed animals
- 🛍️ Shop local and choose products from the islands
- 💧 Save water — in the Canaries it's a scarce resource
- 📵 Keep quiet in natural spaces — other beings live here

*Travelling well is also part of the experience.*

pois.name: Punta de Teno
pois.shortDescription: Tenerife's westernmost tip — a volcanic headland where the Atlantic breaks against the cliffs of the Teno Massif, with a historic lighthouse, crystal-clear waters and the finest views of La Gomera and La Palma
pois.description:
**Punta de Teno** is the westernmost point of Tenerife and one of the most singular and emotionally powerful places on the entire island. At the extremity of the **Teno Massif** — the oldest part of Tenerife at over 7 million years old —, the headland juts into the Atlantic between black basalt cliffs, impossible turquoise waters and a silence broken only by the wind and the sea. Here Tenerife ends. And here the Atlantic begins.

### The Landscape
Arriving at Punta de Teno is arriving at the end of the world in the best possible sense. The TF-445 road descends between sheer cliffs above the sea, depositing the traveller in a small space where everything converges:
- 🏔️ The **Teno cliffs** of black basalt — wild and imposing, plunging vertically into the ocean
- 🌊 The **Atlantic** in a deep turquoise that contrasts dramatically with the black rock
- 🏝️ The small **black pebble beach** at the foot of the headland — peaceful, sheltered, of austere beauty
- 🏛️ The **Punta de Teno Lighthouse** — one of the most beautiful lighthouses in the Canaries, white against black volcanic rock
- 🌬️ The constant northwest wind, sculpting the cardón cacti and vegetation into extraordinary forms

### The Views
From Punta de Teno unfolds one of the most spectacular panoramas in the archipelago:
- 🏝️ **La Gomera** — the neighbouring island, so close it seems touchable, with the Roque de Agando and the Garajonay massif perfectly recognisable
- 🏔️ **La Palma** — on the northwest horizon when conditions allow, its unmistakable caldera profile clear against the sky
- 🌊 The **La Gomera Strait** — the waters separating the two islands, often with pilot whales (*Globicephala macrorhynchus*) and dolphins
- 🏔️ The **Cliffs of Los Gigantes** — Teno's great basalt wall to the south, visible from the headland looking southeast

### The Lighthouse
The **Punta de Teno Lighthouse** was built in **1897** and has been guiding sailors through the passage between Tenerife and La Gomera for over 125 years. Its white tower against the black volcanic rock is one of the most iconic images of northwest Tenerife and one of the most sought-after photographs by island visitors. The lighthouse remains operational today.

### The Sea and Marine Wildlife
The waters off Punta de Teno belong to the **North Tenerife Marine Reserve**, ensuring exceptional water quality and remarkable marine biodiversity:
- 🐬 **Short-finned pilot whale** (*Globicephala macrorhynchus*) — permanently resident in the waters between Tenerife and La Gomera. Whale-watching excursions depart from Los Gigantes, but sightings from the headland are also possible
- 🐢 **Loggerhead sea turtle** (*Caretta caretta*) — passes through these waters during Atlantic migrations
- 🐟 **Exceptionally rich seabed**: groupers, white seabream, octopus, moray eels, angel sharks
- 🐦 **Royal tern** (*Thalasseus maximus*) and **Cory's shearwater** (*Calonectris borealis*) soaring above the headland

### The Vegetation
The headland's surroundings display the characteristic vegetation of Tenerife's arid northwest:
- 🌵 **Canarian cardón** (*Euphorbia canariensis*) — the columnar cacti populating the cliffs
- 🌿 **Tabaiba amarga** (*Euphorbia regis-jubae*) — greyish shrub adapted to salt spray
- 🌱 **Verol** (*Aeonium* spp.) — the succulent rosettes growing in rock crevices
- 🌴 **Canarian palm** (*Phoenix canariensis*) — solitary in the most sheltered hollows

### Access: Shuttle Bus or on Foot
Access to Punta de Teno is special. The road is **closed to private traffic** most of the time, which has perfectly preserved the site:
- 🚌 **Official shuttle bus** from the Buenavista del Norte car park — the main means of access
- 🥾 **On foot** along the road or via the **coastal path** descending from Buenavista (≈ 3.5 km, 1.5 h)
- 🚗 Private car access only during very limited hours (check the Cabildo website)

### Practical Information
- 📍 Punta de Teno, Buenavista del Norte — western tip of Tenerife
- 🚌 Shuttle from Buenavista: check current timetables on the Cabildo de Tenerife website
- 💶 **Free access** (shuttle may have a reduced fee)
- 🕙 **All day** — sunset is especially magical
- ⏱️ Recommended duration: **2–3 hours**
- 🌬️ Very windy area — bring a jacket even in summer
- 🏊 Swimming possible on the pebble beach, but watch for currents

### Recommendation
Arrive at sunset. The last sun illuminates La Gomera and transforms the ocean into a mirror of oranges and reds as the lighthouse begins its white flashing signal. It is one of the most powerful moments in the Tenerife experience — and one of the most remembered by those who live it. If you can, combine it with a walk through the village of **Buenavista del Norte**, the quietest and most authentic in the island's northwest.

---

🌿 **Responsible tourism in the Canary Islands**
Canarian ecosystems are unique in the world. Small gestures make a big difference:

- 🚶 Stick to marked trails and don't access restricted areas
- 🗑️ Leave no trace — take back what you bring
- 🐋 Keep your distance from wildlife and don't feed animals
- 🛍️ Shop local and choose products from the islands
- 💧 Save water — in the Canaries it's a scarce resource
- 📵 Keep quiet in natural spaces — other beings live here

*Travelling well is also part of the experience.*

municipios.name: Santa Cruz de Tenerife
municipios.shortDescription: The island's capital and one of the Canaries' most vibrant cities — Atlantic port, world-famous Carnival, Calatrava's Auditorio and an authentic urban life far from mass tourism.
municipios.description:
**Santa Cruz de Tenerife** is the island's capital and one of the archipelago's most dynamic cities. A major Atlantic port, it blends colonial and contemporary architecture, high-quality urban gastronomy and a cultural life that peaks each year at the **Santa Cruz Carnival** — declared a Festival of International Tourist Interest and considered one of the three biggest carnivals in the world.

### What to see in Santa Cruz
- 🎭 The **Auditorio de Tenerife** by Santiago Calatrava — architectural icon on the Atlantic waterfront
- 🌴 The **Palmetum** — the most complete palm collection in Europe
- 🏛️ The **Museum of Nature and Archaeology (MUNA)** — the world's most important Guanche collection
- 🌿 **Parque García Sanabria** — the largest urban garden in the Canaries
- ⛵ The **Port of Santa Cruz** — one of the busiest cruise ports in the Atlantic
- 🏰 The **Castillo de San Juan Bautista** — 17th-century colonial fortress

### Is Santa Cruz worth visiting?
**Absolutely.** Santa Cruz is the most authentic face of Tenerife — one that lives apart from the mass tourism of the south. Its blend of modernity, history, culture and gastronomy makes it an essential stop.

### Recommendation
Devote at least half a day. Start at the Auditorio at dawn, continue to the Palmetum and finish with lunch at one of the city centre markets. If you coincide with Carnival (February–March), book months in advance.

municipios.name: San Cristóbal de La Laguna
municipios.shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage City and Tenerife's first capital — the most complete historic centre in the Canaries, with colonial churches, centuries-old universities and a unique youthful, university energy.
municipios.description:
**San Cristóbal de La Laguna** is Tenerife's most historic city. A **UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999**, it was the first capital of the Canary Islands and the urban model that influenced the layout of many Latin American cities. Its historic centre is the most complete and best-preserved in the Canaries.

### What to see in La Laguna
- 🏛️ The **Cathedral of La Laguna** — Gothic-Neoclassical with a richly ornamented interior
- ⛪ The **Cristo de La Laguna** — Tenerife's most venerated image
- 🏰 **Casa Lercaro** — 16th-century Renaissance palace housing the History Museum
- 🌿 **Calle San Agustín** — the most distinguished street in the old quarter, lined with manor houses
- 🔭 The **Museum of Science and the Cosmos** — with planetarium
- 🎓 The **University of La Laguna** — the oldest in the Canaries, founded in 1792

### Is La Laguna worth visiting?
**Without doubt.** It's the perfect cultural counterpoint to tourist Tenerife. Its grid-plan historic centre with 16th-century palaces is a walk through Canarian history.

### Recommendation
Explore on foot: the historic centre is compact and pedestrianised. Combine with the tram from Santa Cruz (10 minutes). The aperitivo hour in Plaza del Adelantado is a local ritual worth experiencing.

municipios.name: La Orotava
municipios.shortDescription: The most beautiful municipality in the Orotava Valley — 17th-century manor houses, flower carpets at Corpus Christi, Spain's oldest Botanical Garden and the best views of Mount Teide from the north.
municipios.description:
**La Orotava** is, for many, Tenerife's most beautiful municipality. Perched above the fertile **Orotava Valley** with Teide dominating the horizon, it preserves a historic centre of manor houses with carved wooden galleries and balconies from the 17th century that make it one of the most photogenic towns in the Canaries.

### What to see in La Orotava
- 🌺 The **historic centre** — cobbled streets lined with 16th–17th-century palaces and manor houses
- 🌿 The **Botanical Garden of Puerto de la Cruz** — Spain's oldest, founded in 1788 by Charles III
- 🎨 **Flower and volcanic sand carpets** — every Corpus Christi, floral mosaics fill the streets for days
- 🏛️ The **Church of La Concepción** — 18th-century Canarian Baroque
- 👁️ The **Humboldt Viewpoint** — the valley and Teide views that made the German naturalist famous

### Is La Orotava worth visiting?
**Absolutely essential.** It's the finest historic centre in northern Tenerife and the most authentic on the island for colonial Canarian architecture.

### Recommendation
Visit during Corpus Christi (May–June) for the flower carpets. At any other time, the historic centre deserves at least two hours of unhurried exploration.

municipios.name: Puerto de la Cruz
municipios.shortDescription: Tenerife's most historic tourist destination in the north — cosmopolitan, green and Atlantic, with César Manrique's Lago Martiánez, Loro Parque and a unique blend of tourism and local life.
municipios.description:
**Puerto de la Cruz** is northern Tenerife's most iconic tourist destination and one of the Canaries' tourism pioneers. It has maintained its own urban identity: characterful streets, quality gastronomy, historic architecture and a local life that coexists naturally with tourism.

### What to see in Puerto de la Cruz
- 🌊 **Lago Martiánez** — designed by César Manrique, saltwater pools beside the Atlantic
- 🦜 **Loro Parque** — one of Europe's finest zoos
- 🌿 The **Botanical Garden** — Spain's oldest, with over 3,000 tropical species
- ⚫ **Playa Jardín** and **Playa de Martiánez** — the best beaches in the north
- 🏛️ The **historic centre** — Plaza del Charco and the colonial lanes

### Is Puerto de la Cruz worth visiting?
**Yes, especially if you're looking for Tenerife's green north.** It pairs perfectly with La Orotava and excursions to Teide from the north via TF-21.

### Recommendation
At dawn, the Lago Martiánez reflecting a snow-capped Teide in winter is an image few forget. Allow at least two days to explore Puerto de la Cruz and its surroundings properly.

municipios.name: Adeje
municipios.shortDescription: Tenerife's most important tourist municipality in the south — Playa de las Américas, Costa Adeje, the Barranco del Infierno and international-class hotels and gastronomy.
municipios.description:
**Adeje** is Tenerife's most important tourist municipality and one of Spain's most visited destinations. Its coastline boasts the island's finest hotel infrastructure, fine sandy beaches, an almost always sunny climate and a leisure, gastronomy and activity offering that makes it a complete destination.

### What to see in Adeje
- 🏖️ **Costa Adeje** and **Playa de las Américas** — the great tourist beach of the south with full services
- 🌿 The **Barranco del Infierno** — the south's only permanent waterfall, in a 400-metre canyon
- 🐬 **Whale-watching excursions** from Puerto Colón — among the best in the world
- 🏘️ The **village of Adeje** — historic mountain village with the Santa Úrsula church and Casa Fuerte
- 🍽️ Puerto Colón gastronomy — some of the south's finest fish restaurants

### Is Adeje worth visiting?
**It's the epicentre of southern Tenerife.** For beaches, quality dining and water activities, Adeje is your perfect base. The Barranco del Infierno adds the natural dimension.

### Recommendation
Pair the beach side with the Barranco del Infierno (advance booking required) and a whale-watching excursion from Puerto Colón.

municipios.name: Arona
municipios.shortDescription: Guaranteed sunshine, Los Cristianos and Las Galletas — Tenerife's most animated and accessible southern municipality, with family beaches, ferries to La Gomera and year-round tourist life.
municipios.description:
**Arona** is one of the most dynamic municipalities in southern Tenerife. With over **5 million visitors a year**, it combines family beaches, an active port, leisure options for all and an exceptional climate throughout the year.

### What to see in Arona
- ⛴️ **Los Cristianos** — the south's busiest port, with ferries to La Gomera and El Hierro
- 🏖️ **Las Galletas** and **Costa del Silencio** — quieter beaches with less crowding
- 🏘️ The **village of Arona** — historic mountain village at 600 m altitude with southern views
- 🌋 The **Malpaís de Rasca** — volcanic lava nature reserve by the sea
- 🐬 Whale-watching excursions from Los Cristianos

### Is Arona worth visiting?
**For travellers seeking beaches and active tourist life, it's an excellent base.** The ferry connection to La Gomera opens up some very interesting day-trip options.

### Recommendation
Use the Los Cristianos connection for a day trip to **La Gomera** — Garajonay National Park and Valle Gran Rey are just 50 minutes away by ferry.

municipios.name: Garachico
municipios.shortDescription: The most beautiful village in northern Tenerife — a volcanic stone historical gem on the Atlantic, with natural lava pools, a 16th-century fortress and an irresistible tranquillity.
municipios.description:
**Garachico** is the most beautiful and best-preserved village in northern Tenerife. Until 1706 it was the island's most important port. That year, a volcanic eruption buried the port under lava, and what seemed a tragedy became the village's most singular legacy: the solidified lava created the **Caletón Natural Pools** — seawater pools in volcanic rock that are now the most photographed attraction in the north.

### What to see in Garachico
- 🌊 The **Caletón Natural Pools** — volcanic lava pools with Atlantic water
- 🏰 The **Castillo de San Miguel** (16th century) — perfectly preserved black basalt fortress
- 🏛️ The **historic centre** — stone streets with convents, churches and colonial manor houses
- ⛪ The **Church of Santa Ana** — one of the most beautiful temples in the north
- 🌿 **Parque de Puerta de Tierra** — botanical garden where Humboldt rested during his visit

### Is Garachico worth visiting?
**One of the most recommended visits in the north.** It has maintained a human scale and authenticity especially attractive to travellers seeking to avoid mass tourism.

### Recommendation
Visit at midday to swim in the Caletón and explore the historic centre in the afternoon. Pairs perfectly with **Icod de los Vinos** (7 km) and the **Macizo de Teno** viewpoints.

municipios.name: Icod de los Vinos
municipios.shortDescription: Home of Tenerife's Millenary Dragon Tree — the world's oldest and largest specimen of the species, alongside a beautiful wine-growing historic centre and the Mariposario del Drago butterfly house.
municipios.description:
**Icod de los Vinos** is known worldwide for its **Millenary Dragon Tree** — over 800 years old and 17 metres tall, the largest and oldest known specimen of *Dracaena draco*. But beyond the dragon tree, Icod is a wine-growing municipality with an architecturally rich historic centre.

### What to see in Icod de los Vinos
- 🌳 The **Millenary Dragon Tree** — the Canaries' most emblematic tree, in Parque El Drago
- 🦋 The **Mariposario del Drago** — hundreds of exotic tropical butterflies in a garden beside the dragon tree
- 🏛️ The **Church of San Marcos** — one of the finest in the north, with a valuable Baroque interior
- 🍷 Local **wineries** — wines from the D.O. Ycoden-Daute-Isora
- 🏘️ The **historic centre** — streets of manor houses with carved Canarian tea-wood balconies

### Is Icod de los Vinos worth visiting?
**Yes.** The dragon tree alone justifies the visit, but combining it with the butterfly house, the old town and a local winery makes for a very complete experience.

### Recommendation
Visit the Dragon Tree early in the morning to avoid tour groups. Combine with **Garachico** (7 km) and the **Macizo de Teno** route.

municipios.name: Buenavista del Norte
municipios.shortDescription: Tenerife's most tranquil and authentic municipality in the northwest — gateway to the Macizo de Teno, with the spectacular Punta de Teno, wild ravines and a calm that contrasts radically with the south.
municipios.description:
**Buenavista del Norte** is Tenerife's westernmost and one of its most authentic municipalities. Far from the main tourist circuits, it preserves a rural and maritime identity that makes it ideal for travellers seeking old Tenerife. It is the gateway to the **Macizo de Teno** and to **Punta de Teno** — the island's westernmost point.

### What to see in Buenavista del Norte
- 🌊 **Punta de Teno** — Tenerife's westernmost cape, with the historic 1897 lighthouse and views to La Gomera and La Palma
- 🌿 The **Macizo de Teno** — Tenerife's oldest terrain (7 million years)
- 🏘️ The **village of Buenavista** — peaceful agricultural village with a historic church
- 🌊 **Buenavista beach** — small, quiet and genuinely authentic
- 🥾 **Teno hiking trails** — routes through cliffs, ravines and xerophytic vegetation

### Is Buenavista del Norte worth visiting?
**Absolutely, especially for nature lovers.** Punta de Teno at sunset is one of Tenerife's most memorable experiences.

### Recommendation
Reach Punta de Teno on the shuttle from Buenavista car park (the road is closed to private traffic). Combine with a Macizo de Teno hiking route.

municipios.name: Santiago del Teide
municipios.shortDescription: Gateway to the Macizo de Teno and Masca Gorge — a mountain municipality on western Tenerife with one of the island's most spectacular volcanic landscapes and the Cliffs of Los Gigantes at its feet.
municipios.description:
**Santiago del Teide** is a mountain municipality on Tenerife's western flank, between the **Macizo de Teno** and the towering basalt wall of the **Cliffs of Los Gigantes**. It is the access point to the **Masca Gorge** — the island's most epic hiking route — and Los Gigantes harbour, one of the best whale-watching spots in European waters.

### What to see in Santiago del Teide
- 🏔️ The **Masca Gorge** — 5 km descent through a 300-metre canyon to a virgin cove
- 🌊 The **Cliffs of Los Gigantes** — black basalt walls up to 800 metres high, the tallest in Europe
- 🏘️ The **Hamlet of Masca** — one of Tenerife's most remote and beautiful villages
- 🐋 **Los Gigantes harbour** — excursions to spot pilot whales and dolphins
- 🌿 **La Ensillada Nature Reserve** — protected area with endemic flora

### Is Santiago del Teide worth visiting?
**Essential for the adventurous traveller.** The Masca Gorge and Los Gigantes together offer Tenerife's most complete adventure day.

### Recommendation
Book the Masca Gorge in advance (limited, regulated access) and combine with a boat trip from Los Gigantes. Seeing the cliffs from above and from the sea is a transformative experience.

municipios.name: Guía de Isora
municipios.shortDescription: Tenerife's southwest municipality with the clearest skies — home to the Izaña Observatory, the black beaches of Alcalá and the Royal Hideaway Corales Hotel, one of Europe's finest.
municipios.description:
**Guía de Isora** is a southwest Tenerife municipality combining spectacular volcanic scenery, an uncrowded Atlantic coastline and the island's finest astronomical visibility. The **Izaña Observatory**, at 2,400 metres altitude, is one of the world's most important astronomical facilities.

### What to see in Guía de Isora
- 🔭 The **Izaña Observatory** — IAC facility with world-class telescopes
- 🏖️ **Alcalá harbour and beach** — authentic fishing village with a dark-pebble beach
- 🏖️ **Los Gigantes Beach** — the volcanic black beach at the foot of the cliffs
- 🌅 **Southwest sunsets** — the island's finest, with La Gomera on the horizon
- 🏨 The **Royal Hideaway Corales Hotel** — one of Europe's most award-winning five-star properties

### Is Guía de Isora worth visiting?
**Yes, especially for astronomy enthusiasts.** Stargazing from Izaña is an experience hard to match anywhere in Europe.

### Recommendation
Book a night visit to Izaña Observatory in advance — places are limited and demand is high. Combine with sunset at Alcalá with La Gomera in the background.

municipios.name: Granadilla de Abona
municipios.shortDescription: Home of El Médano and its legendary wind — world capital of windsurfing and kitesurfing with the red Montaña Roja as a backdrop, and the gateway to Tenerife South Airport.
municipios.description:
**Granadilla de Abona** is a southern municipality whose greatest attraction is **El Médano** — the island's windiest town and one of the world's premier windsurfing and kitesurfing destinations. Its fine sandy beaches with the volcanic silhouette of **Montaña Roja** as a backdrop create a landscape of great beauty.

### What to see in Granadilla de Abona
- 🏄 **El Médano** — world mecca for windsurfing and kitesurfing, with kilometres of fine sandy beach
- 🌋 **Montaña Roja** — red volcanic cone by the sea, a Special Nature Reserve
- 🏘️ The **El Médano village** — charming beach village with terraces and a relaxed atmosphere
- 🌊 **Leocadio Machado and El Cabezo beaches** — the windsurfers' favourites
- ✈️ **Tenerife South Airport** (TFS) — the island's busiest

### Is Granadilla de Abona worth visiting?
**For water sports enthusiasts and travellers seeking authenticity in the south, yes.** El Médano has a far more relaxed and authentic atmosphere than Adeje or Arona.

### Recommendation
If you don't windsurf, the walk between El Médano and Montaña Roja at sunset, when colourful sails fill the horizon, is a very special visual experience.

municipios.name: San Miguel de Abona
municipios.shortDescription: The deep south of Tenerife — Los Abrigos and the south's finest fresh fish, Tenerife Karting and the most residential and authentic face of the southern tourist coast.
municipios.description:
**San Miguel de Abona** is a southern municipality combining consolidated tourist zones with tranquil, authentic corners. Its coastline, between **Los Abrigos** and **Las Galletas**, concentrates high-quality fresh fish restaurants and small fishing harbours that have maintained their original character.

### What to see in San Miguel de Abona
- 🐟 **Los Abrigos** — one of the south's best fishing villages for fresh seafood straight from the harbour
- 🏁 **Tenerife Karting Club** — the largest go-kart circuit in the Canaries
- 🏖️ **Las Galletas** — small fishing harbour with a quiet beach and authentic local atmosphere
- 🌅 The **San Miguel village** — historic mountain village at 600 metres with southern views

### The gastronomy of Los Abrigos
Los Abrigos is famous throughout Tenerife for its seafood and fresh fish — grilled limpets, red prawns, grouper and parrotfish cooked in traditional style. One of the south's finest gastronomic destinations.

### Is San Miguel de Abona worth visiting?
**Yes, especially for the gastronomy of Los Abrigos.**

### Recommendation
If you're in the south, don't leave without eating in Los Abrigos. Portions are generous and the fresh catch of the day is exceptional.

municipios.name: Candelaria
municipios.shortDescription: Tenerife and the Canaries' spiritual capital — the Basilica of Our Lady of Candelaria, patron of the archipelago, beside bronze statues of the nine Guanche kings on the seafront promenade.
municipios.description:
**Candelaria** is the spiritual capital of Tenerife and the entire Canarian archipelago. **Our Lady of Candelaria**, patron of the Canary Islands, was the first Marian image found in the Canaries before the Spanish conquest. The **Basilica of Candelaria** is the most important religious centre in the entire archipelago.

### What to see in Candelaria
- ⛪ The **Basilica of Our Lady of Candelaria** — the most important temple in the Canaries, by the sea
- 🗿 The **nine bronze Guanche mencey statues** — sculptures of the aboriginal kings of Tenerife
- 🌊 The **seafront promenade** — one of the most beautiful on eastern Tenerife
- 📜 The **Museum of Traditions** — history of the Virgin's devotion and Guanche culture

### Is Candelaria worth visiting?
**Yes, especially if you're interested in the islands' history and spirituality.**

### Recommendation
Visit at any time, but **2 February** (the Virgin's feast day) or **15 August** (the Assumption pilgrimage) are particularly moving dates when thousands of pilgrims from across the Canaries fill the square.

municipios.name: Güímar
municipios.shortDescription: Tenerife's most intriguing archaeological mystery — the Pyramids of Güímar studied by Thor Heyerdahl, in a fertile eastern valley with the island's sunniest and most temperate microclimate.
municipios.description:
**Güímar** is an eastern Tenerife municipality known worldwide for its **Pyramids** — six stepped stone structures that Norwegian explorer **Thor Heyerdahl** (famous for the Kon-Tiki expedition) identified as intentional constructions with astronomical alignments. The debate about their origin makes Güímar one of the most enigmatic visits in the Canaries.

### What to see in Güímar
- 🔺 The **Pyramids of Güímar** — stepped structures with solstice alignments in the Ethnographic Park
- 🌋 The **Güímar Valley** — a fertile valley with a particularly sunny microclimate
- ⛪ The **Church of San Pedro Apóstol** — historic temple in the town centre
- 🌊 The **east coast** — quiet coves and little-known natural pools

### Is Güímar worth visiting?
**Yes, especially for archaeology enthusiasts.** The Ethnographic Park is one of the most complete on the islands, with a Kon-Tiki raft replica included.

### Recommendation
Combine the pyramid visit (morning) with the MUNA in Santa Cruz (afternoon) for a complete day of Canarian archaeology.

municipios.name: El Sauzal
municipios.shortDescription: Tenerife's wine capital — the Casa del Vino in a 17th-century hacienda with views of Teide and the Atlantic, and the finest wines of the D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo.
municipios.description:
**El Sauzal** is a small northern Tenerife municipality with a very clear identity: wine. Located in the heart of the **D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo**, it houses the **Casa del Vino** — the island's reference space for discovering and tasting its wines.

### What to see in El Sauzal
- 🍷 The **Casa del Vino de Tenerife** — wine museum, tastings, shop and restaurant in a 17th-century hacienda
- 🌊 The **El Sauzal viewpoint** — panoramic views over the Atlantic and northern coast
- ⛪ The **Church of San Pedro** — historic temple in the town centre
- 🍇 Local **wineries** — several family wineries offering tastings

### Is El Sauzal worth visiting?
**For wine tourism, it's the most important visit in the north.** The Casa del Vino has the island's finest wine selection under one roof.

### Recommendation
Visit the Casa del Vino at lunchtime: the terrace restaurant overlooking the Atlantic and Teide is one of the north's finest dining settings.

municipios.name: Tacoronte
municipios.shortDescription: The cradle of Tenerife wine — the municipality that gives its name to the island's oldest D.O., with centuries-old wineries, a deeply venerated Christ and the Park of the Peoples of America.
municipios.description:
**Tacoronte** is the municipality that gives its name to the **D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo**, Tenerife's oldest and most recognised wine denomination. It combines a winemaking tradition dating to the 16th and 17th centuries with an equally deep religious devotion: the **Cristo de Tacoronte** is one of the north's most venerated images.

### What to see in Tacoronte
- 🍷 **Historic wineries** — some of the oldest in the archipelago, with visits and tastings
- ⛪ The **Cristo de Tacoronte** — 17th-century Baroque image of great popular devotion
- 🌿 The **Park of the Peoples of America** — historic garden commemorating ties with the Americas
- 🌊 **Roque de las Bodegas** — beautiful small fishing cove on the northern coast

### Is Tacoronte worth visiting?
**For wine tourism, yes.** Together with El Sauzal, it forms the heart of northern Tenerife's wine culture.

### Recommendation
Combine a winery visit in Tacoronte with the Casa del Vino in El Sauzal and La Laguna's historic centre for a complete cultural and wine day in the north.

municipios.name: Arico
municipios.shortDescription: The south's municipality with Europe's finest climbing conditions — Arico's volcanic rocks are an international bouldering and sport climbing destination in a landscape of stark, arid beauty.
municipios.description:
**Arico** is a southern Tenerife municipality whose greatest international draw is **sport climbing**. The volcanic rocks and walls of the municipality offer some of Europe's finest climbing routes, with over 500 lines in scenically beautiful settings and optimal temperatures year-round.

### What to see in Arico
- 🧗 **Climbing rocks** — Canaries' finest sport climbing and bouldering walls, frequented by climbers from across Europe
- 🏘️ The **historic centre of Arico** — a whitewashed village of great authenticity in the south
- 🌊 The **east coast** — quiet, uncrowded coves
- 🌋 The **Malpaís de Arico** — raw and beautiful volcanic landscape

### Is Arico worth visiting?
**For climbers, it's a world-class destination.** For others, the volcanic landscape of the south has its own appeal.

### Recommendation
If you climb, plan several days in Arico — the density and quality of the routes justifies it. Combine with El Médano for a complete east and south itinerary.

municipios.name: San Juan de la Rambla
municipios.shortDescription: A small maritime municipality in the north with the most beautiful natural pools on Tenerife's north coast — La Rambla de Castro and Las Aguas, turquoise water coves amid volcanic rock.
municipios.description:
**San Juan de la Rambla** is one of Tenerife's smallest municipalities, yet it hides some of the north coast's most beautiful coastal corners. Its **natural pools** between lava and the Atlantic are exceptionally beautiful and relatively unknown outside the local area.

### What to see in San Juan de la Rambla
- 🌊 **La Rambla de Castro Natural Pools** — turquoise water pools amid black basalt cliffs
- 🌊 **Las Aguas Natural Pools** — one of the north's most secret and beautiful spots
- 🏘️ The **village of San Juan de la Rambla** — whitewashed village on the northern cliffs
- 🐟 The **fishing harbour** — small and authentic, with local boats

### Is San Juan de la Rambla worth visiting?
**For lovers of the north's hidden corners, absolutely.** Its natural pools are among the island's most beautiful with very little crowding.

### Recommendation
Visit the pools on a weekday morning. Combine with **Garachico** (15 km) for a complete day along the north coast.

municipios.name: Los Silos
municipios.shortDescription: The northwest's most tranquil and natural municipality — on the doorstep of the Macizo de Teno, with Los Silos' black beach, the Charco del Viento pool and a calm that makes it the north's most authentic corner.
municipios.description:
**Los Silos** is one of Tenerife's smallest and most authentic municipalities, on the far northwest at the gateway to the **Macizo de Teno**. Its small coastal village, dark-sand beach and rhythm completely removed from mass tourism make it one of the north's most special corners.

### What to see in Los Silos
- 🌿 The **Charco del Viento** — beautiful natural pool in lava by the sea
- ⚫ **Los Silos beach** — dark sand and authentic fishing village atmosphere
- 🏘️ The **village centre** — white and intimate, with a central square and local terraces
- 🦋 The **Macizo de Teno** surroundings — endemic flora and volcanic landscapes minutes away

### Is Los Silos worth visiting?
**For travellers seeking authenticity and tranquillity in the north, yes.**

### Recommendation
Visit the Charco del Viento first thing in the morning. Combine with **Garachico** (15 km) and the **Macizo de Teno** viewpoints for a day through the authentic northwest.

municipios.name: Vilaflor de Chasna
municipios.shortDescription: Spain's highest village and the southern gateway to Teide through ancient pine forests — at 1,400 metres altitude, with the island's purest air and the famous Pino Gordo, a centuries-old Canarian pine.
municipios.description:
**Vilaflor de Chasna** is Spain's highest municipality, at over **1,400 metres altitude** on Teide's southern slopes, surrounded by one of the island's densest and most majestic Canarian pine forests. Its privileged position between the South Coast and Teide National Park makes it the ideal starting point for hiking routes to the summit from the south.

### What to see in Vilaflor
- 🌲 The **Pino Gordo** — an extraordinary centuries-old Canarian pine declared a Natural Monument, on the road to Teide
- 🏘️ The **historic centre** — quiet mountain village with a colonial church
- 🥾 **Routes to Teide** — trails rising from 1,400 m up to the National Park boundary
- 🌲 The **Vilaflor pine forest** — one of Tenerife's most spectacular *Pinus canariensis* forests
- ☁️ **Sea of clouds from above** — Vilaflor's position above the cloud layer often allows views over the clouds

### Is Vilaflor worth visiting?
**Absolutely, especially in summer.** The contrast between the hot, bustling south and the cool, serene mountain of Vilaflor is one of Tenerife's most striking contrasts.

### Recommendation
If you're heading up to Teide from the south via TF-21, stop in Vilaflor to see the Pino Gordo and have breakfast in the village. The mountain air and pine forest in the early morning are the perfect preparation for the volcano ascent.

municipios.name: Arafo
municipios.shortDescription: A tranquil eastern Tenerife municipality between the sea and Teide — known for its traditional festivals, mid-altitude farming and access to the ravines of the Güímar Valley.
municipios.description:
**Arafo** is an eastern Tenerife municipality set in the mid-altitude zone between the coast and Teide National Park. With a deeply agricultural and rural identity, Arafo preserves the traditions of mid-altitude Tenerife: vines, potatoes and fruit grown on volcanic terraces, deeply rooted local festivals and a landscape of ravines and pines ideal for quiet hiking.

### What to see in Arafo
- 🌿 The **Güímar Valley ravines** — hiking trails through volcanic ravines with native flora
- 🏘️ The **village of Arafo** — authentic mid-altitude village with traditional rural Canarian architecture
- ⛪ The **Church of San Juan Bautista** — historic temple in the town centre
- 🌾 **Terraced farmland** — the mid-altitude agricultural landscape characteristic of eastern Tenerife

### Is Arafo worth visiting?
**Yes, for travellers seeking rural, mid-altitude Tenerife.** Arafo is an authentic municipality that lives outside mass tourism.

### Recommendation
Combine with **Güímar** (5 km) — the pyramids and the valley together offer a complete day through authentic eastern Tenerife.

municipios.name: El Rosario
municipios.shortDescription: The municipality closest to Tenerife North Airport — a residential district on the outskirts of Santa Cruz, home to Los Rodeos Airport and the maritime neighbourhood of Igueste de Candelaria.
municipios.description:
**El Rosario** is a residential municipality in northeast Tenerife, bordering Santa Cruz de Tenerife. It houses **Tenerife North Airport (Los Rodeos)** — the island's historic airport, primarily for inter-island flights — and offers access to quiet coastal and ravine areas.

### What to see in El Rosario
- ✈️ **Tenerife North Airport (Los Rodeos)** — the historic airport, mainly for inter-island connections
- 🌊 **Igueste de Candelaria** — coastal neighbourhood on the Candelaria border with a quiet beach
- 🌿 The **northeast ravines** — rural hiking trails through ravines and farmland
- 🏘️ The **El Rosario centre** — residential municipality on Santa Cruz's outskirts

### Is El Rosario worth visiting?
As a destination in its own right, its main value is the North Airport connectivity and proximity to Santa Cruz de Tenerife.

municipios.name: El Tanque
municipios.shortDescription: The greenest and quietest municipality in the northwest — a small mid-altitude village between Garachico and Icod with views of Teide and the sea, farmland and exceptional tranquillity.
municipios.description:
**El Tanque** is one of Tenerife's smallest municipalities, set in the northwest mid-altitude zone between **Garachico** and **Icod de los Vinos**. At an average altitude of 600–800 metres, it enjoys a green, humid microclimate that nurtures high-quality agriculture and landscapes of great natural beauty.

### What to see in El Tanque
- 🌱 The **mid-altitude landscape** — farmland, orchards and vineyards in a scenically beautiful setting
- 👁️ **Northwest viewpoints** — panoramic views towards Teide, Garachico and the Atlantic
- 🏘️ The **village of El Tanque** — small and quiet, with authentic rural Canarian architecture
- 🌲 **Ravines and trails** — hiking routes through ravines and farmland

### Is El Tanque worth visiting?
**As a stop en route between Icod and Buenavista del Norte, yes.** Its views and tranquillity make it special for travellers who enjoy authentic Tenerife.

### Recommendation
Include El Tanque as a stop on the northwest route: **Icod de los Vinos → El Tanque → Garachico → Buenavista del Norte → Punta de Teno**.

municipios.name: Fasnia
municipios.shortDescription: A municipality on Tenerife's volcanic southeast — the Fasnia Ravine, a chapel carved into the rock and a malpaís coastline that was the last area to cool after historic eruptions.
municipios.description:
**Fasnia** is one of Tenerife's least-known municipalities, on the southeast coast in an area of significant geological importance. Historic lava flows have created a **coastal malpaís** of raw beauty here, with dark cliffs over the Atlantic and a geology that testifies to the island's recent volcanic activity.

### What to see in Fasnia
- 🌊 The **southeast malpaís coast** — solidified lava fields reaching the sea
- ⛪ The **Ermita de Fasnia** — small chapel carved into volcanic rock, of great singularity
- 🌋 The **Fasnia Ravine** — one of the southeast's ravines of greatest geological interest
- 🏘️ The **village of Fasnia** — small, quiet and genuinely authentic

### Is Fasnia worth visiting?
**For volcanic geology enthusiasts and seekers of unknown southeast corners, yes.** Fasnia is one of Tenerife's most authentic and least-crowded municipalities.

### Recommendation
Combine with **Arico** and the southeast coast for a day along the island's most volcanic and least-touristed coastline.

municipios.name: La Guancha
municipios.shortDescription: The deep north municipality between pines and banana plantations — a quiet and authentic mid-altitude village between Los Realejos and Icod, with spectacular Atlantic views from the northwest highlands.
municipios.description:
**La Guancha** is a mid-altitude municipality in northwest Tenerife, between **Los Realejos** and **Icod de los Vinos**. With a historically agricultural economy and a strongly rural identity, La Guancha is one of the north's most authentic and least-visited municipalities.

### What to see in La Guancha
- 🌾 **Terraced farmland** — the banana plantation and orchard landscape that defines the northwest
- 👁️ **Mid-altitude viewpoints** — panoramic views over the Atlantic and northern coast
- 🏘️ The **village of La Guancha** — mid-altitude village with authentic rural Canarian architecture
- 🌲 **Northwest trails** — hiking routes through ravines and pine forests

### Is La Guancha worth visiting?
**As a stop en route between Los Realejos and Icod, yes.** Its views and tranquillity make it special for travellers who enjoy rural Tenerife.

### Recommendation
Include La Guancha as a stop on the route to Icod de los Vinos and the Macizo de Teno. The mid-altitude views at sunset are particularly beautiful.

municipios.name: La Matanza de Acentejo
municipios.shortDescription: The site of the famous 1494 battle where the Guanches defeated the Castilian troops — a northern wine village amid D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo vineyards and Atlantic viewpoints.
municipios.description:
**La Matanza de Acentejo** takes its name from one of the most important episodes of Tenerife's conquest: in 1494, Guanche warriors under mencey Bencomo defeated the Castilian army of governor Alonso Fernández de Lugo in the **First Battle of Acentejo** — the greatest Guanche victory of the conquest. The municipality is part of the **D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo**.

### What to see in La Matanza de Acentejo
- ⚔️ The **historic battlefield** — where the Guanches defeated the conquerors in 1494
- 🍷 **D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo vineyards** — high-quality wines grown on volcanic soils
- 👁️ **Northern viewpoints** — panoramic views over the Atlantic and Teide
- 🏘️ The **village centre** — mid-altitude village with rural Canarian architecture

### Is La Matanza de Acentejo worth visiting?
**For Canarian history enthusiasts and wine tourism, yes.** The historical context of the battle and the Acentejo vineyards create a singular combination.

### Recommendation
Combine with the neighbouring **La Victoria de Acentejo** and the **Casa del Vino** in El Sauzal for a complete history and wine day in northern Tenerife.

municipios.name: La Victoria de Acentejo
municipios.shortDescription: The site of the 1495 historical revenge — where Castilian troops avenged the La Matanza defeat and opened the way to the definitive conquest of Tenerife, now a northern wine corner.
municipios.description:
**La Victoria de Acentejo** takes its name from the opposite episode to its neighbour La Matanza: in 1495, the Castilian forces of Alonso Fernández de Lugo defeated the Guanches here in the **Second Battle of Acentejo**, opening the way to the definitive conquest of Tenerife. The municipality is part of the **D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo**.

### What to see in La Victoria de Acentejo
- 🏆 The **historic context of the Second Battle of Acentejo** (1495) — the Castilian revenge that opened the conquest
- 🍷 **D.O. Tacoronte-Acentejo vineyards** — high-quality red and white wines
- 👁️ **Northern viewpoints** — views over the Atlantic and coast
- 🏘️ The **village centre** — mid-altitude village with rural Canarian architecture

### Is La Victoria de Acentejo worth visiting?
**As a historical stop on the north route, yes.** Together with La Matanza it forms an essential historical diptych for understanding Tenerife's conquest.

### Recommendation
Visit La Matanza and La Victoria de Acentejo together to grasp the full arc of the conquest story. Add a local winery to complete the day.

municipios.name: Los Realejos
municipios.shortDescription: The municipality of northern natural pools and Spain's most spectacular fireworks — a maritime municipality between Puerto de la Cruz and Garachico with decades of pyrotechnic tradition.
municipios.description:
**Los Realejos** is a northern Tenerife municipality between **Puerto de la Cruz** and **Garachico**, with a stunning volcanic coastline. It is known for its **natural pools** on the north coast and its legendary **San Juan fireworks** — considered some of the finest and most spectacular in Spain, with decades of pyrotechnic tradition.

### What to see in Los Realejos
- 🌊 **North coast natural pools** — lava pools beside the Atlantic
- 🎆 **San Juan fireworks** (24 June) — one of Spain's most impressive pyrotechnic displays
- 🏘️ The **historic centre** — the municipality has two distinct nuclei (Realejo Alto and Realejo Bajo)
- 🌿 **Northern ravines** — hiking trails through ravines and farmland in the highlands

### Is Los Realejos worth visiting?
**For the San Juan fireworks, absolutely.** One of Spain's most impressive pyrotechnic spectacles.

### Recommendation
If you're visiting Tenerife around 24 June, don't miss the Los Realejos fireworks. At other times, the north coast natural pools are a good reason to visit.

municipios.name: Santa Úrsula
municipios.shortDescription: The balcony of the Orotava Valley — a mid-altitude municipality with privileged panoramic views over Tenerife's most fertile valley and Teide in the background, among vineyards and orchards.
municipios.description:
**Santa Úrsula** is a mid-altitude municipality in northern Tenerife that enjoys some of the most privileged views over the **Orotava Valley** — the island's most fertile and picturesque valley, with Teide dominating the horizon. Its mid-altitude position, at between 300 and 600 metres, gives it a mild microclimate and lush vegetation.

### What to see in Santa Úrsula
- 🌄 **Views over the Orotava Valley** — privileged panoramas towards Teide and the valley
- 🌿 **Mid-altitude vineyards and orchards** — the agricultural landscape that defines the north
- 🏘️ The **village of Santa Úrsula** — mid-altitude village with rural Canarian architecture
- 🥾 **Highland trails** — routes between the valley and the summits with spectacular views

### Is Santa Úrsula worth visiting?
**As a viewpoint and stop between Puerto de la Cruz and La Orotava, yes.** Its views over the valley are among Tenerife's finest.

### Recommendation
Stop in Santa Úrsula on the journey between Puerto de la Cruz and La Orotava. At sunset, with Teide turning orange above the green valley, the views are spectacular.

municipios.name: Tegueste
municipios.shortDescription: The north's smallest wine municipality — on La Laguna's doorstep, with vineyards on volcanic soils, centuries-old wineries and the most authentic rural character in the Santa Cruz–La Laguna metropolitan area.
municipios.description:
**Tegueste** is the smallest municipality in the northern comarca and one of Tenerife's most singular. Just a few kilometres from **San Cristóbal de La Laguna**, it preserves a completely rural character: its vineyards on volcanic soils produce some of the north's most interesting wines, and its local festivals maintain traditions that have been lost in other municipalities.

### What to see in Tegueste
- 🍷 **Vineyards and wineries** — small family wineries producing wines of great character
- ⛪ The **Church of San Marcos** — historic temple in the town centre
- 🏘️ The **village of Tegueste** — the most authentic village near La Laguna
- 🌿 **Ravines and trails** — hiking routes through ravines and vineyards in the north

### Is Tegueste worth visiting?
**For wine tourism and travellers seeking authenticity near La Laguna, yes.** Tegueste is rural Tenerife just 10 minutes from a UNESCO World Heritage city.

### Recommendation
Combine a winery visit in Tegueste with an afternoon in **La Laguna**'s historic centre (10 minutes by car). The perfect blend of rural and historic Tenerife.
